This page needs cleanup, restyle, or its contents are significantly outdated.You can help clean it up by updating this page and bringing it up to wiki standard.

Biomes O' Plenty also adds custom achievements, all of which are just picking up blocks from certain biomes, like red rock, glowflower, etc.  There's also a set of "Biome Finder" achievements that you get for entering all of the different biomes.  They're just meant to give people more of a reason to explore and have fun.

Contents

1 
2 Flower Child - Become one with nature!
3 North Branch

3.1 Movin' On Up! - Welcome to the Promised Land!
3.2 Blue Sky - I am the one who...blocks...
3.3 Drink of the Gods - Stay thirst, my friends.


4 East Branch

4.1 Flower Power - Groovy, man.
4.2 Full Auto - You'll shoot your eye out, kid!
4.3 Plant KIller - The grim reaper's day job.
4.4 Home Sweet Home - Use the magical powers of the Enderporter.


5 South Branch

5.1 Bittersweet - The land of blood and honey.
5.2 Decay - A master of disguise
5.3 Gravedigger - The next Dampe.
5.4 Phantom Menace - Stealer of souls...


6 West Branch

6.1 Berry Picking - The simple things in life...
6.2 A Rolling Stone - It gathers none of this.
6.3 Rather Thorny - Deadlier than cacti!
6.4 Nutritious - How about a big piece of steamed coral?


7 Achievements o' Plenty



[edit]
Disclaimer: These achievements were recorded in Minecraft 1.6.4. It is entirely possible that they could have changed since then. If you do not see an achievement in your game that is listed here, it is likely that it was removed.

Flower Child - Become one with nature![edit]
To unlock this achievement you must pick a flower from the world, simple.

North Branch[edit]
Movin' On Up! - Welcome to the Promised Land![edit]
To unlock this achievement you must go through a portal found in the sky after using an Ancient Staff on the ground.
You will be taken to the Promised Land. Please note that the Promised Land caused too much lag and was consequently removed.

Blue Sky - I am the one who...blocks...[edit]
You must aquire a Celestial Crystal Shard from breaking part of a Celestial Crystal, commonly found on the underside of the Promised Land.

Drink of the Gods - Stay thirst, my friends.[edit]
You must craft a bottle of Ambrosia from: pixie dust, honey jar, water bottle, kelp, miner's delight, berry, root, celestial crystal shard and sugar.

East Branch[edit]
Flower Power - Groovy, man.[edit]
You must craft a Dull Flower Band from eight Clovers in a ring formation.

Full Auto - You'll shoot your eye out, kid![edit]
You must craft a Dart Blower with six river cane in a ring formation minus the top-centre and bottom-centre.

Plant KIller - The grim reaper's day job.[edit]
Simply craft a Scythe with two sticks to the right side, two tool material at centre top and top-right and centre-left. Upon crafting the Scythe you will be given the achievement. By 'tool material' it means wood, cobblestone, iron, gold, amethyst, ect.

Home Sweet Home - Use the magical powers of the Enderporter.[edit]
As it implies, you must craft an Enderporter with an Amethyst in the middle and four eyes of ender in each corners, filling in the remaining spaces with Ghastly Souls. Upon using the Enderporter you will be rewarded with the achievement.

South Branch[edit]
Bittersweet - The land of blood and honey.[edit]
To get this achievement, you must go to the Nether and find a hive hanging from the Nether's roof. You must break into the hive and find a Filled Honeycomb Block. Break this and an item will drop. Collect this item and you will be rewarded with the achievement. Be warned, as breaking into the Hive will spawn Wasps which will promptly attack you and possibly knock you off into lava or death by falling.

Decay - A master of disguise[edit]
Staying in the Nether, you must find a Wither Wart in an Undergarden biome. They will be hidden inbetween regular Nether Wart. Wither Warts are distinguishable by a slightly darker tone than their Nether Wart brethren. It is recommended you break the block underneath the Wither Wart, as that way you will not recieve the Wither effect and still pick up the Wither Wart.

Gravedigger - The next Dampe.[edit]
You must find a Gravestone in the Nether and break it. Once you collect the item it drops you will be rewarded with the achievement.

Phantom Menace - Stealer of souls...[edit]
Occasionally as you explore the Nether you will be attacked by what appears to be nothing. Look out for particles and attack that. If you kill the Phantom it will drop a Ghastly Soul. Pick that up and recieve the achievement.

West Branch[edit]
Berry Picking - The simple things in life...[edit]
Find a bush that has grown berries and right click on them to recieve a berry and this achievement.

A Rolling Stone - It gathers none of this.[edit]
Find a piece of moss, usually found in a Fen biome on a tree. Break this moss, pick up the item and receive this achievement.

Rather Thorny - Deadlier than cacti![edit]
Go to the nether, and find a Thorns plant growing on Soul Sand. Break these with Shears and pick up the item. You will be given the achievement promptly.

Nutritious - How about a big piece of steamed coral?[edit]
Underwater you will occasionally find coral reefs. Break a piece of coral and pick up the item to collect your achievement.

Achievements o' Plenty[edit]
Recieve this after completing all the Biomes o' Plenty achievements. This serves as a token to your dedication. Congratulations.

Flower Child[edit]
Find a flower![edit]
Pick a Biomes O' Plenty flower.

Berry Good[edit]
Pick a berry from a berry bush[edit]
Destroy or right-click a berry bush to get the berry.

Totally Coral![edit]
Dive deep for some coral[edit]
Find coral in a Coral Reef biome. It can also be achieved by finding and harvesting algae.

Life finds a way[edit]
Find a miner's delight flower deep within a cave[edit]
Find and harvest a miner's delight.

Getting a Downgrade[edit]
Build a...muddy pickaxe...?[edit]
Craft a pickaxe using two sticks and three balls of mud.

Rather Thorny[edit]
Collect a prickly thorn![edit]
Use shears to harvest a thorn bush.

Trippin'[edit]
Ingest some magical shroom powder[edit]
Use a crafting table to make shroom powder from toadstools.

Honeycomb's Big[edit]
Steal a filled honeycomb from a Nether Wasp Hive[edit]
Find a Hive in the nether and destroy a Filled Honeycomb Block.

Pick Your Poison[edit]
Extract poison from a Poison Ivy plant[edit]
Craft poison using a poison ivy plant and an empty bottle.

Flaxen Fun[edit]
Craft flax plants into flax string[edit]
Fill the crafting table with flax plants to make string.

Your Powers Combined[edit]
Combine all 8 biome-specific gems together[edit]
Combine amber, emerald, topaz, ruby, peridot, sapphire, malachite, and tanzanite with a crafting table to make a Terrestrial Artifact.

Don't Breathe This[edit]
Kill a pixie and harvest its magical dust[edit]
Find a Pixie in a Mystic Grove biome and kill it.

Godsend[edit]
Rescue a wilted lily flower[edit]
Find and collect a Wilted Lily.

Search Party[edit]
Use the biome finder to locate a biome[edit]
Craft a biome finder and use Biome Essence to find a biome.

Stalk Market[edit]
Harvest a turnip[edit]
Use turnip seeds from Koru plants to grow and harvest a turnip.

I am Become Death[edit]
Acquire a deadly Deathbloom[edit]
Find a Deathbloom in the Ominous Woods biome.

Far Out...[edit]
Mine a Celestial Crystal in the End[edit]
Find a Celestial Crystal in the End and break it to collect the shards.

Soul Searching[edit]
Reclaim a lost Soul[edit]
Collect a Soul.

Special Achievements[edit]
These are the rare achievements with spikey borders for their boxes in the achievement gui.

True Swordsman[edit]
Upgrade to an amethyst sword[edit]
Find Amethyst in the End and combine it with an iron ingot to make a sword

Yggdrasil[edit]
Plant a Sacred Oak sapling[edit]
Find a Sacred Oak sapling in a Sacred Springs biome or loot chest.

The Wanderer[edit]
Truly discover all biomes[edit]
Find all Biomes O' Plenty Biomes.

Nectar of the Gods[edit]
Sugar, water, honey, berries, roots, kelp, ichor, pixie dust, and celestial crystals![edit]
Combine all elements on a crafting table to create ambrosia.

Gone Home[edit]
Travel to the origin point with an Enderporter[edit]
Use an Enderporter to go back to the original spawn point.

Trivia[edit]
Many of these achievements returned from older BOP versions.
The "Totally Coral!" achievement name could be a reference to a saying in a Spongebob Episode.
The "Life finds a way" achievement name is a reference to Jurassic Park.

Algae is one of the few ocean blocks in the mod. It can usually be found in large naturally generated biomes with water. Algae can't be broken with lava, flint & steel, fire, or any content from other mods.

Looks:[edit]
Algae has the same effect of slowing you down as walking into a large strip of water in Minecraft. Its appearance is notably similar to seagrass.

Algae needs specific conditions to be placed, but I do not know these at the time of writing.

The Alps consist of a single mountainous landmass, specifically the base and the highest, flattest part of the area. The upper-middle region of the mountain generally (though not always) consists of an Alps Foothills sub-biome, which is an entirely different location in itself. Along with its sub biome, it was removed in 1.18 due to the terrain generation changes making the biome invalid.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Natural Hazards
1.2 Vegetation & Spring Water
1.3 Mobs & NPCs
1.4 Survival


2 Changelog
3 Trivia
4 Gallery

4.1 Current
4.2 Old





Description[edit]
The lower part of the Alps generally consists of a very steep, almost entirely vertical upwards incline. The bottom tends to display a few features from neighboring biomes, with stone and snow eventually replacing them as the elevation increases.
With regard to the peaks, there are deep layers of snow with no features whatsoever excusing occasional pools and pockets of (usually frozen) water. Alps Foothills biomes often generate on or near Alps peaks, providing a source of wood and mobs.
The Alps soar much higher than the cloud layer, at around y=200, and they are flat on the top. It is a cold biome.
Did you also know that there is a special liquid in this biome called Spring Water? It is a type of liquid that spawn in very few biomes including the Alps. If you stand in it, it will give you the regeneration effect.

Natural Hazards[edit]
The Alps are incredibly high. Even falling from a peak to the foothills, about two-fifths of the total fall can prove to be deadly. Caves or empty pockets can also be hidden by the snow, causing you to fall in if you dig below the snow layer.

Vegetation & Spring Water[edit]
There is no vegetation in this biome, other than subterranean fungi. However, there may be fir trees scattered around the nearby Alps Foothills. Spring water can be found in underground caves in this biome as well.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs don't spawn in the Alps biome itself but may spawn in the Alps Foothills and find their way up the mountain. These mobs are primarily llamas, but sheep can occasionally be found here. Skeletons and strays are also really common in the Alps at night.

Survival[edit]
The Alps biome contains only the bare necessities for survival; food and wood are both present and replenishable, yet scarce; zombies do not spawn, so rotten flesh cannot be used as a food source; the trees in the Alps Foothills biome usually generate on stone, meaning you cannot replant them without bringing grass blocks from other biomes or from a lower part of the mountain; the plain terrain and lack of natural cover leave you open to attacks from large groups of mobs.

Changelog[edit]


Biomes o' Plenty Version

Changes


Build 1.7.2-2.0.0.482

Alps were apparently 'readded'. The original addition date is unknown due to the gaps in the official changelog.


Build 1.7.2-2.0.0.801

The "Alps Forest" sub-biome was added. The biome is not currently in BOP, and it is unknown what has happened to its files.


Build 1.7.2-2.0.0.804

Tweaks and bug fixes


Build 1.8-3.0.0.1115

"Initial Implementation". It is unknown what is meant by this, as earlier changelog versions already mentioned the addition and editing of the Alps.


Build 1.8-3.0.0.1118

"Initial Implementation" (???) mentioned again.


Build 1.8-3.0.0.1197

Emerald generation was added to the Alps.


Build 1.8.9-3.0.0.1827

The amount of snow on the Alps was increased.


Build 1.9.4-4.1.0.2043

The amount of hot springs in the Alps, along with other biomes, was tweaked.


Build 1.11.2-6.1.0.2240

The possibility of the Cold Beach spawning adjacent to the Alps was removed.


Build 1.11.2-6.1.0.2248

The Alps Foothills sub-biome was added.

Trivia[edit]
In real life, the European Alps are one of the great mountain range systems of Europe. The highest peaks of the Alps are higher than 4,000 meters (the highest peak is Mont Blanc or Monte Bianco with its 4,810 meters high).
There is also a mountain range in New Zealand called the Southern Alps, because of the resemblance to the European Alps. It was the filming location of the Misty Mountains scene from the live-action film adaptation of Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring.
Some other biomes can be as high or almost as high (crag, mesa) as the alps biome, though are not covered with snow.
The Biome ID before 1.8 was 173
The original appearance of the Alps consisted of a massive landmass crowned by trees and a thin layer of snow. A more recent appearance had thicker snow and lacked trees. As of the most recent update, the Alps are generally no longer flat; They are more dynamic in height and tend to have an Alps Foothills biome, yielding a decent supply of wood.
The Alps used to have lots of hot spring water, which would give players an extremely strong regeneration effect.

The Alps Foothills are a sub-biome of the Alps biome that was added in a Biomes o' Plenty update for Minecraft 1.11.2. It spawns around the taller Alps mountains, reaches to about the cloud layer, has Overgrown Stone covered in snow as its surface block, and is dotted with Fir trees. Along with its parent biome, it was removed in 1.18 due to the terrain generation changes making the biome invalid.

Survival[edit]
This biome is easier to survive in compared to its parent biome, since this sub-biome has some fir trees scattered around that provides you with some wood to build a house, but it is hard to find food, because sheep are the only food-dropping mob. It is recommended that you bring supplies and animals from other biomes so that you may create a farm. It is not suggested that you live in the Alps or the Foothills because of the limited resources and isolation.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
An Altar Frame is crafted using four Obsidian and five Large Bone Segments. It is used as part of the multi-block structure to summon an Ender Dragon.
As of BOP for 1.6.4, this has all been removed. Respawnable Ender Dragons were later introduced in vanilla Minecraft 1.9, by using End Crystals.

Recipe[edit]


Summoning an Ender Dragon[edit]
Capture a Villager with a Soul Manipulator.
In The End place four Altar Frame blocks as shown (this view is from overhead).


You will need four of each of the Biomes O' Plenty gems (Ruby, Peridot, Apatite (Malachite v1.2.0+), Topaz, Sapphire and Tanzanite). Place one of each type in each Altar Frame. The side of each Altar Frame will look like this when complete:


Place the Sacrificial Focus in the center of the structure as shown (this view is from overhead).


On the top of each Altar Frame, place a Medium Bone Segment. On top of each of the Medium Bone Segments, place a Small Bone Segment.
Use a Ghastly Soul Manipulator on the Sacrificial Frame.
Right-click on the Sacrificial Frame with the Villager Soul Manipulator.
Use another Ghastly Soul Manipulator on the Sacrificial Frame. This will cause the entire structure to explode and an Ender Dragon to appear.

Generation[edit]
Amber Ore can be discovered in forest biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Amber Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Amber Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Amber drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Amber Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Amber can be crafted into a Block of Amber for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.Notes: Removed in Minecraft 1.10.2

Amethyst armor was crafted from Ender Amethyst, and was stronger than diamond armor. Amethyst armor had 640 durability and in early versions it was reportedly protective to such a degree that players became near invulnerable. Previous to 1.7.2, Amethyst armor was crafted from Amethyst that was found in the Promised Land. Amethyst armor has been repeatedly nerfed as its protection was first lowered and then Amethyst was gated behind the End rather than the more accessible and populated Promised Land dimension. It was removed in 1.10.2.

Recipes[edit]
Amethyst Helmet, Amethyst chestplate, Amethyst legging, Amethyst boots.

		NormalDepleted
	
		
			
				
					
					
				
			
		
		
			
				
					
					
				
			
		

	Ancient Staff


The Ancient Staff was used to reach the Promised Land. But as of Biomes o' Plenty version 7.17, the Promised Land is no longer in game, and many of the blocks contained there have been completely removed. The Ancient Staff exists in some versions of 1.7, but it doesn't serve any purpose.

Traveling to the Promised Land[edit]
  Ancient Staff recipe
Once a staff is made, using it in the hotbar will create a structure in the sky above you that contains a portal to the Promised Land. Afterwards the staff will become depleted and will need to be recharged with a nether star in a crafting grid.

Gem Spawns/Locations[edit]
Rubies can be found in Desert Biomes
Topaz can be found in Jungle and Tropical Biomes
Peridot can be found in Grassland Biomes
Malachite can be found in Swamp Biomes
Sapphire can be found in Oceanic Biomes
Such as Mangrove
Tanzanite can be found in Snow Biomes (taiga)
Emeralds can be found in the Alps biome. (not just Extreme Hills)

Apatite is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O' Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and as a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use
4 Crafting Ingredient
5 History



Generation[edit]
Apatite Ore can be found in some biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Apatite Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
A pickaxe is required to mine Apatite Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Apatite drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Apatite Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Apatite can be crafted into a Block of Apatite for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

Crafting Ingredient[edit]
History[edit]
Apatite was removed in 1.8.

The Arctic was a biome in Biomes O' Plenty. Before 1.5.2, it was a forest with fir trees, but after 1.5.2, it was a snowy wasteland with no trees or tallgrass. Only hostile mobs spawned in this biome, although villages could be found in it. A sub-biome of this biome is the Glacier biome.
Evidently, the Arctic does not currently exist. Its sub-biome, the Glacier, can be found near vanilla Ice Plains.

Contents

1 Climate
2 Deformities
3 Description

3.1 Climate
3.2 Known deformities


4 Survival Tactics

4.1 Suggested Resources
4.2 Suggested Method


5 Trivia
6 Gallery



Climate[edit]
The Arctic Biome was a very cold biome and sat at the approximate elevation of a vanilla Plains biome.

Deformities[edit]
The Arctic had no known unique generation glitches.

Description[edit]
The arctic biome is an extremely flat and desolate biome, only interrupted by the occasional glacier and frozen river. It is completely covered in snow and is without any tall grass or passive mobs. The overall desolate and inhospitable nature of this biome is comparable with the Wasteland biome.

Climate[edit]
The Arctic sits at about the general height of the Plains. It is cold and snowy.

Known deformities[edit]
The Arctic does not have any unique glitches.

Survival Tactics[edit]
Suggested Resources[edit]
Saplings - If living here, you're going to need a source of trees (unless you live on the edge of the biome, where there may be trees from another biome).
Wood - You're going to need some wood to begin building; Saplings may take a while to grow.
Food source - Bring animals or seeds. I suggest bringing seeds as animals require you to feed them, breed them, and cook their meat. Seeds require less resources; you need water. If it's frozen, simply use a torch!
Suggested Method[edit]
Simply use the resources listed above to survive. Use your wood to build a shelter, prepare your food source, and plant your saplings. It's not a very good way of life, but if you are smart with limited rations than it will turn out fine. Zombies can also provide Rotten Flesh for food after night passes.

Trivia[edit]
In real life, the Arctic biome corresponds to a variant of taiga, with tall trees and scattered forest. In places like Northern Alaska and Siberia, these areas are tundra with no trees or tall grass.

Blocks of Ash (or simply Ash Blocks) are dark gray blocks found in Deadlands, Volcanic Island, and Phantasmagoric Inferno biomes.
They drop four ash when broken, and have a smoke-like particle effect above them. The resulting ash can be used in a furnace resulting in 2 smelting processes per item making them as efficient as coal. Also, you can craft coal by putting it into a crafting table in a 3x3 pattern.

  Ash to Coal
You can also use ash to create Gray Dye. One block of ash will create two bowls of Gray Dye.

History[edit]
In 1.12.2-7.0.1.2352, players and mobs no longer have a slowdown on this block. In 1.16.1, Ash Blocks were removed because Vanilla Minecraft introduced Basalt.

  Ash to Gray Dye

The Ashen Inferno is a Biome created in the Nether. It mostly consists of Ash Blocks. This biome is one of the most useful Nether biomes added by Biomes O' Plenty, as the Ash can be crafted into coal or be used as fuel in a furnace. You can easily spot this biome by the huge amount of Ash Blocks. Before 1.11.2, Smoldering Grass Blocks were used instead of Magma Blocks. Blue Fire now appears in this biome, along with regular fire. Blue Fire gives the curse effect when stepped into.

Versions[edit]
As of early April, 2016, Nether Biomes have not be re-added to 1.9 and 1.8.9 BoP, though the programmers are planning to bring them back. They are in 1.7.10 and earlier, though.
However, in version 1.11.2+ all nether biomes except Boneyard are readded to BOP.
Blue Fire was added to this biome as of Biomes O' Plenty version 1.12.2-7.0.1.2361.
As of 1.12.2-7.0.1.2350, magma blocks no longer generate in this biome.
In 1.13.2, this biome was renamed to Ashen Inferno.
In 1.16.1, this biome was removed in favor of the Basalt Deltas biome from Vanilla Minecraft.

The Aspen Glade is a boreal biome filled with unique pear-shaped birch trees containing yellow maple leaves and yellow maple trees. The biome is also scattered with yellow maple leaf piles, barley, and toadstools. It generates relatively common near other colder biomes, such as the Coniferous Forest or Seasonal Forest. Fallen birch logs can be found with leaf piles and toadstools on top of them. Poppies and dandelions can sometimes be spotted in this biome.

History[edit]
In versions 1.16.3 and under, the biome was named Boreal Forest
In version 1.16.4 the biome was renamed again to the Seasonal Orchard
In versions 1.20 and under the biome's trees were yellow autumn trees.
In version 1.20.1 it was finally renamed to the Aspen Glade and removed the yellow autumn trees for the unique tree it has now

The Auroral Garden is a considerably rare biome that contains rainbow birch and fir trees. It has no hostile mobs, and violets, icy irises, and grass cover the landscape. The grass is frosted, and snow covers the landscape. This biome has plenty of wood, and the passive mobs provide food, making it a good biome to live in. It will often spawn near a Mushroom Field and Frozen Ocean, which is why it is so rare. Previous versions of the Auroral Garden, before 1.18, had no snow, bluish-green grass, and lots of flowers---and prior to 1.19.2, it was an island biome.

History[edit]
It was added in 1.15.1, being the rarest biome in the entire game. It was previously known as Rainbow Hills, and then Rainbow Valley. 
Before its release, the Origin Valley was the rarest biome.

The Autumn Hills biome featured jutting hills punctuated by soaring firs, Persimmon Trees, the occasional dead fell, and rough ground cover. The grass was a very muddy green verging on brown, and the sky was a vibrant blue. In a BoP update that made the mod compatible with Minecraft 1.7.2, the Autumn Hills were removed.

Contents

1 Vegetation
2 Mobs & NPCs
3 Survival

3.1 Recommended Resources:
3.2 Recommended Strategy:


4 Changes



Vegetation[edit]
Fir Trees, Oak Trees, Dead Trees, and Persimmon Trees
The underbrush included tall grass, regular grass, Wheat Grass, Poison Ivy and thorns.
Pumpkins spawned here more often than other forest-hills style biomes.
Bushes spawned less commonly here, but almost all of them contained berries that grew back fast.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Sheep, pigs and cows spawned here. Small groups of pumpkins could be found here. Pink sheep could spawn here in large groups, but they were a rare find.

Survival[edit]
Recommended Resources:[edit]
- None; They're all here.

Recommended Strategy:[edit]
The Autumn Hills were just like any other forest biome in Minecraft, with the exception of hills and natural hazards (Thorns and Ivy). Survive here like you would in a vanilla Minecraft forest.

Changes[edit]
This biome was removed after BoP 1.2.0 (Minecraft 1.6.4).

The Badlands are extremely dry (like the Desert biome) and hilly (like the Extreme Hills biome). Its surface is covered mainly by uncolored hardened clay, but also a considerable amount of clay, red hardened clay and orange hardened clay. No vegetation or friendly mobs spawn here. This biome has a blue sky with hints of yellow. Ravines will spawn here often, so bring along boots enchanted with Feather Falling if you are scared of falling into one by accident. Tanzanite spawns here. You will also find an exceptional amount of gold very close to the surface and in mineshafts just under hills.

Contents

1 Vegetation
2 Mobs & NPCs
3 Early Survival
4 Interesting Strategies
5 Trivia
6 Gallery - Current version
7 Previous Version



Vegetation[edit]
Dead bushes are the only vegetation that spawns naturally in the Badlands.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive Mobs do not spawn in this biome. The hilly nature of the terrain and its impressive overhangs make it dangerous due to mobs staying around during the day. But NPC villages spawn here, they are the main source to survive.

Early Survival[edit]
Survival is extremely hard in this biome. Lack of water, grass, villages and trees makes it almost impossible to find food and make tools. The only ways to find food naturally there is by either killing zombies and eating rotten flesh (which can cause hunger), or mine to try to find dirt underground and wood from an abandoned mineshaft. If a player wants to make their home in the Badlands biome, they will have to import dirt, seeds and saplings from elsewhere to be able to survive properly.

Interesting Strategies[edit]
Survival is nearly impossible in this biome; food is hard to come by, one major suggestion is to bring some seeds and dirt with you when you attempt to survive here. Otherwise, you'll be dead after a while; to pass time while not draining your hunger bar, use a bed to skip the nights, and your hunger bar will not deplete while you are sleeping, keeping you alive for possibly a few more days. Summary: Survival is hard without seeds in this biome, don't try it.

Trivia[edit]
In real life, a badland is a biome made of sedimentary rocks, extremely dry and eroded by water and/or wind. It generally displays a specific colors due to the oxidation of the sedimentary rocks with the water that used to flow there.
The yellowish sky of badlands may represent sand particles that are suspended in the air because of the wind.
The Mesa biome from the vanilla game is renamed to "Badlands" as of 1.13.

Bamboo are found in the Bamboo Forest . When the bottom block is mined the entire tree falls. Bamboo trees yield bamboo stalks instead of blocks of raw wood. The stalks can be used as sticks or to craft Bamboo thatch blocks. There are no bamboo slabs or stairs.
When bamboo stalks are planted on dirt or grass, they behave almost like sugar canes, but they do not need water sources.
The bamboo stalk grows until it is 3 blocks tall, it will not become a bamboo tree. In 1.9.4 the texture was changed so they are now more green rather than yellow. However, should you want to start a bamboo forest of your own, they act like trees in the way that breaking their leaves has a chance of dropping bamboo saplings.
NOTE: Since 1.14 bamboo has been added into the game. This will most likely be removed in later versions of the mod.

Raw wood: Bamboo
Planks: Bamboo Thatch (has to be crafted)
Crafting: no slabs, no stairs

The Bamboo Forest biome is a forest of tall Bamboo Trees that overlook a flat, vibrant land with shrubs, bushes, and ferns. This Biome is different from the Bamboo Jungle that was added to vanilla Minecraft in 1.14, as that biome is a jungle variation but not a bamboo forest

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
Bamboo Forest is a flat biome with ground made of large patches of both Podzol and Grass blocks. Tall bamboo trees (20 blocks high) soar above, while the ground is covered in grasses, ferns and dense oak shrubs.

Vegetation[edit]
Dandelions, Poppies, Tall Grass, and Bushes. Leaf Piles also occur, and Berry Bushes can provide a small amount of food, although they spawn infrequently here.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
The only Passive mob is the panda but all others appear absent, and villages do not spawn, meaning only hostiles are likely to be creeping about.

Survival[edit]
Surviving in this biome is quite easy, despite some small difficulties. Finding food won't be very hard for the player, as ferns can give seeds just like grass. Bamboo can be crafted into a Bamboo Thatching for building, or used in place of sticks.
This biome is a little crowded. Wandering about at night is a very bad idea. Mobs can hide behind the trees or around the bushes, therefore ambushes are sure to occur, so it would be wise to not go out at night.

History[edit]
Prior to 1.11.2, dense oak shrubs appeared in this biome.

Trivia[edit]
In real life, bamboo forests are native to Eastern Asia, in countries like China, Korea, Japan.
In real life, newly grown bamboo can be eaten, though Biomes O' Plenty doesn't give the possibility of that.
Before 1.8 the Biome ID was 174.
Bamboo has been officially added in 1.14, in their own biomes called bamboo jungles and bamboo jungle hills

In the Bayou biome, overcast skies overlook a lush swampy area with tall willow trees with hanging spanish moss. The Bayou can be divided into two parts: water and land. The ground of the land part is made of dirt and is covered by Grass, Mud, and few Mushrooms. Cattails spawn around the biome, and ferns are found very frequently. Villages do not spawn here, although Witch Huts can. Slimes can also be found above ground in this biome. Squids spawn in the water. Surviving in this biome can be pretty easy. It has a large amount of wood, and a lot of grass to get seeds.
There was a sub-biome, Deep Bayou, a deeper version of the bayou, however this was removed in 1.18 due to the generation changes making the biome invalid.

Trivia[edit]
Bayou, in real life, is the name given in USA for swamp wetlands in Louisiana and Texas.
Before 1.8, the biome ID was 27.
Bayou biome is one of the swamp/wetland biome with the least amount of water.

Biome Essence
	
		
		
	
	

	Biome Essence

		Type
	Crafting Ingredient

		Renewable
	No

		Stackable
	Yes

		ID №
	4245


A Biome Essence is an item that you can craft with a Biome Finder to help you find the location of a desired biome. 

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Generation
3 Crafting
4 Usage
5 History
6 Gallery



Obtaining[edit]
As of the 1.8.9 update, Biome Essence Ore can be mined in the End to acquire Biome Essence. The Biome Essence Ore drops 1-2 random Biome Essences.
It can also be found in loot chests in dungeons and mineshafts [needs verification]
It can be summoned by using the command /give @p biomesoplenty:biome_essence 1 0 {biomeID:###} Replace the ### with the proper ID of the biome you wish to find.
Generation[edit]
Biome Essence Ore generates in veins in the End with a vein size of 1-2. They generate near the bottom of the central island where you fight the dragon. They will also generate on the Outer Islands in the End Highlands biome.

  
  Distribution pattern as seen with X-Ray mods
Crafting[edit]
Once crafted with a Biome Finder, the Finder becomes permanently fixed to locate the biome indicated by the Essence. The Biome Essence must have a specified biome or else the Finder cannot be crafted. The Biome Essence provided in Creative mode does not have a biome specified and will not work.

  A Biome Essence used to create a fixed Biome Finder
Usage[edit]
Once crafted, the Biome Finder will point you to the nearest biome of the type contained in the Essence. However, it doesn't always lead you to the nearest biome, it only locates biomes within a 14,000 block radius. Similar to a compass, if you turn so that the purple light is at the top and go in that direction, you will find the aforementioned biome. If there is no matching biome within 14,000 blocks, the light will not turn on.

  A Biome Finder in use
History[edit]
When it was first added, it had a different texture, resembling a yin yang. This was changed to dust in 1.8. It was removed in 1.13.2 and higher.

The Biome Finder is able to find specified biomes with a detection radius of 13045 blocks (proof is in the gallery).

Contents

1 Crafting
2 Use
3 Notes
4 History
5 Gallery



Crafting[edit]
A Biome Finder requires four Ender Amethysts and one Terrestrial Artifact.  Crafting recipe for the Biome Finder
Use[edit]
A Biome Finder requires biome essence to function. A specific Biome Essence is crafted with the Biome Finder to create a Fixed Biome Finder for the biome specified by the essence. (i.e. a Desert biome essence will create a desert Biome Finder.) To change the biome, craft the Biome Finder with another essence. Make sure to remember to use the Biome Essence, or else it wont work. 

  A desert biome essence used to craft a desert biome finder.
Notes[edit]
A standard biome essence (lacking any identification of a biome) cannot be used to craft a fixed Biome Finder.
If a biome is not in range the console will display the message: Not found, maybe [Biome] is too far away.
  A Biome Finder in use
History[edit]
When it was introduced, it was called Biome Radar, and had a completely different texture, resembling a real green radar. It also had a different crafting recipe. In 1.8, it was renamed to Biome Finder, texture was changed and the crafting recipe was also changed. In 1.13.2 and upwards, it was removed completely.

content:
Listed are some of the many biomes that you can discover with Biomes O' Plenty.
Although the Mod states there are around 60-90 biomes (depending on what version you're using), there are over 110 ".class" files which are used to generate the biomes. Some of them are the Terrain Generations, nerfing the vanilla biomes also give another class files, so it's basically 87 biomes is correct without the vanilla biome nerfed and the Terrain Generations. Technical biome also counts, including beaches replaced by gravels, ponds etc.

content:
This page uses many images.Loading may be slow on some browsers or lower-end devices.

See also: Biomes Index
This page lists all of the biomes in this mod. Temperatures are as follow: Snowy biomes have their temperature listed in purple, cold in blue, temperate in green, arid in orange, and the nether in red. The biomes of either neutral or unknown temperature have no temperature class.

Contents

1 Overworld Biomes
2 Nether Biomes
3 End Biomes
4 Removed Biomes



Overworld Biomes[edit]


Biome Name

Features

Rarity

Description

Image


Aspen Glade

None

None

A hilly biome with yellow-like grass and Barley coverage. Ferns and other grassy plants. Aspen Trees spawn all over the place, made up of birch and yellow maple leaves.

  


Auroral Garden

Temperature: -0.25
Downfall: 0.5


Very rare

A biome full of rainbow birch and fir trees. The grass is frosted and icy irises spawn here. No hostile mobs spawn here either.




Bamboo Grove

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.9


Rare

A variant biome of the cherry blossom grove, containing fewer cherry trees, and the addition of bamboo.




Bayou

Temperature: 0.95
Downfall: 0.9


Common

A murky biome with willow trees, based on wetlands from the southern USA. Cattails also spawn around the shore, and ferns cover the ground.




Bog

Temperature: 0.2
Downfall: 0.5


Common

A biome based on the Cranberry Bog. It has lots of bush plants, maple and spruce scrub, as well as reeds.




Cherry Blossom Grove

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.9


Rare

A biome with flowering oak, pink cherry, and white cherry trees. Lots of flowers spawn here, including lilacs, pink daffodils, and peonies.




Cold Desert

Temperature: 0.25
Downfall: 0.0


Uncommon

A wasteland comprised of gravel and powder snow. Some desert grass spawns here, but no passive mobs do.




Coniferous Forest

Temperature: 0.45
Downfall: 0.5


Common

A forest comprised of tall fir trees. Toadstools and various vanilla flowers such as dandelions, cornflowers and poppies litter the surface.




Crag

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.6


Uncommon

Variant biome of the highland with cobblestone, andesite, and stone mixed into the grassy surface. It also has steeper and more jagged terrain.




Dead Forest

Temperature: 0.2
Downfall: 0.3


Uncommon

A sparsely populated forest, with mainly dead trees and spruce trees. Not much grass spawns in this biome either, and no passive mobs spawn.




Dryland

Temperature: 0.85
Downfall: 0.05


Common

A dry landscape with brush oak trees and bushes. Bush plants also cover the surface, and the ground is comprised of both sand and grass blocks.




Dune Beach

Temperature: 0.7
Downfall: 0.4


Common

A vanilla beach biome, but covered in dune grass and sea oats. Rooted sand occasionally replaces the sand in the biome.




Field

Temperature: 0.4
Downfall: 0.7


Common

A pretty flatland with small spruce trees and oak bushes, and a variety of flowers including lilacs, rose bushes and sunflowers.




Fir Clearing

Temperature: 0.45
Downfall: 0.5


Common

Variant of the coniferous forest with sparsely spread small fir trees.




Floodplain

Temperature: 1.2
Downfall: 2.0


Common

A lush wetland with watergrass, orange cosmos, lily pads, and small dripleaves. Brush oaks and bushes spawn here as well.




Forested Field

Temperature: 0.4
Downfall: 0.7


Uncommon

Variant of the Field with more trees and less flowers.




Fungal Jungle

Temperature: 0.9
Downfall: 0.9


Rare

A rainforest comprised of toadstools and huge toadstools, with a fungal green sky color. Jungle trees also spawn here.




Grassland

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.7


Common

A plains biome with more grass, frequent rolling hills and lots of clovers. No flowers or trees spawn here though.




Highland

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.6


Common

An elevated plains biome with lots of tall grass and grass.




Highland Moor

Temperature: 0.6
Downfall: 0.6


Uncommon

Variant of the highland with lots of violets, alliums, and occasional patches of oak leaves.




Hot Springs

Cold

Common

The Hot Springs biome consists of Pine and Spruce trees. Thermal Calcite borders the water.




Jacaranda Glade

Temperature: 0.8
Downfall: 0.7


Uncommon

A biome with large Jacaranda Trees, Flowering Oak Trees, tiny Snowblossom Trees, and Cherryblossom Trees. Blue Orchids and Lilies are also scattered throughout the biome.

Temperature: 0.8
Downfall: 0.85


Rare

A densely forested mountainous biome with spruce trees and bushes. A green sky is present in this biome aswell.

Downfall: 0.7

Downfall: 0.5

Downfall: 0.5

Downfall: 0.275

Downfall: 0.6

Temperature: 0.7

A jungle biome full of mahogany trees. Small and big dripleaves and orange cosmos flowers cover the surface, as well as seagrass and watergrass in the water. Surface of the water can have lilypads.

Temperate

A forest biome chock full of towering redwood trees and ferns. The ground is mostly made up of podzol besides sparse patches of moss blocks.

Warm

Cold

Temperate

Icy

WIP

Icy

Snowy Maple Woods

Icy

Tropics

Warm

Very rare

Tundra

Cold

Common

Volcanic Plains

Warm

Rare

A biome that consists of black sand and some shrubs. No trees spawn here.




Volcano

Warm

Very rare

A rare biome consisting of Black Sand, basalt, magma blocks, and enormous pools of surface lava.




Wasteland

Warm

Uncommon

A dry, dead biome with terrain made of Dried Salt blocks. Features some sparse dead trees.




Wetland

Temperate

Uncommon

A wet, marshy biome with a blue tint to the grass and leaves. Mud lines the banks, and Cattails and Reeds are common here.




Woodland

Temperate

Common

A welcoming oak forest biome rich with both large and small flowers. Fallen oak logs speckle the landscape, and passive mobs are plentiful.

The first version for Biomes O' Plenty for 1.13.2 was released on May 25th, 2019.
In this version, a lot of things were changed, added and removed.

Biomes O' Plenty Wiki 
487 pages • 2,934 files • 36,248 edits

Welcome to the unofficial wiki for Biomes O' Plenty that anyone can edit! We currently have 487 articles and more thanks to all the contributors since January 2013! We've amounted 36,248 edits from our wonderful contributors since then!
Biomes O' Plenty is a Java Edition mod and a Bedrock Edition addon for Minecraft created by Glitchfiend, a collaborative group of two developers, with the Bedrock Edition addon being made by 4KS Studios. The mod/addon adds over 60 new biomes to Minecraft, ranging from a simple Marsh biome, all the way to the magical and mysterious Mystic Grove! Many new things are also added alongside these biomes, such as new trees, building blocks, and plants.
All users are welcome to edit or post comments as long as it is in compliance with the guidelines.


NOTE: This wiki is not supported or endorsed by the developers! Information found here may be inaccurate/outdated, and should not be used as reference for 
issues, bug reports, or any other requests to the developers!

Birch Forest is a simple forest covered in only birch trees.

Contents

1 Description
2 Survival Tactics
3 Interesting Strategies
4 Trivia
5 Gallery



Description[edit]
Birch forest biome is a relatively flat biome. Various types of grasses, poison ivy, clover patches, and poppies can be found scattered on the surface, and the biome is composed of a medium density birch tree forest. Villages by default can spawn in this biome.
Surviving in this biome is easy. The various types of grass provide ample wheat seeds, the large amount of birch wood, and the possibility for villages to spawn allow for more access to resources.
As with all forests, there are minor cons. The trees allow hostile mobs to hide and ambush the player. Building any aboveground structure typically requires to clear cut the area necessary. The poision ivy can poison the player, leaving him or her vulnerable to further damage.

Survival Tactics[edit]
The Birch forest is a really good starting biome because of the large amounts of trees. Sadly you wont get an achievement of punching wood from Birches.
The Survival rating for this biome is an 8/10

Interesting Strategies[edit]
Really? You REALLY need an interesting strategy for a biome as simple as this? Well, the only thing I can point out is that this forest is birch-only. Birch trees are generally the highest trees from original Minecraft. Building a treehouse would be great. Summary: This section isn't very long, stop being lazy and just read the whole thing

Trivia[edit]
Villages spawning in the birch forest biome uses oak wood, even if it cannot be found naturally in this biome.
In real life, birch forests can be found in temperate and some boreal climates of Europe, Asia and North America.
Birch Forest is a popular custom biome in Minecraft and mods. It can be found in ExtraBiomesXL, for example. It is now also found in the official vanilla Minecraft since 1.7.2.

Obtaining[edit]
Can be obtained with any tool or by hand, but using a shovel is the quickest method.
Natural Generation[edit]
Black Sand naturally generates in the Volcanic Plains, Burnt Forest, and Ominous Woods biomes.
Behavior and Physics[edit]
Like most sand blocks, including the White Sand, the Black Sand obeys physics and will fall if no blocks are underneath it.
They can be crafted in all sandstone variants.
like other sand types, the player can plant dead bushes, cactus and Dune Grass on it.

Blood is a fluid that naturally generates in the Visceral Heap in small pools or on the sides of walls.

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Usage

2.1 Contact with Liquids


3 History
4 Gallery



Obtaining[edit]
Blood can only be obtained using a bucket on a existing blood source block, creating a Blood Bucket. There are no other means of obtaining blood, and it does not create infinite sources like water.
Unlike water and lava, blood does have a direct item form, and can be obtained using /give @p biomesoplenty:blood. It is invisible in the inventory.

Usage[edit]
Blood has no practical use other than converting itself and other liquids to Flesh.

Contact with Liquids[edit]
If blood comes into contact with any liquid source, it will immediately turn the source into Flesh. If flowing blood comes into contact with any flowing liquid, it will turn the flowing liquid into Porous Flesh. When blood is seven blocks away from a lava source block, the blood will push back the lava until the source is turned into flesh. If Liquid Null is poured over blood, then all the blood will be turned into Null Blocks.

History[edit]


1.6.4

Blood is added to the mod and functions the same as water.  


1.13.2

Blood is removed from the mod.


1.17.1

Blood is re-added, re-textured, can be walked through without slowing you down, unable to be drowned in, and unable to swim through  


1.19

Blood can slow you down, be drowned in, and is completely see-through when submerged.


1.19.3

Red fog covers the player's screen when submerged in Blood.


1.20.1

The top and bottom of Fluid Blood is re-textured.

Blue fire is a unique variant of Template:MC.
It is distinct from normal fire as it does not burn blocks or entities, nor spreads like normal fire. Instead, it inflicts the Curse Effect for a duration of 10 seconds to entities that touch it including the player.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Natural Generation
1.2 Blue Fire Jar


2 Usage
3 Trivia
4 Gallery



Obtaining[edit]
Natural Generation[edit]
Blue fire naturally generates in Template:MC across the terrain of the Phantasmagoric Inferno.

Blue Fire Jar[edit]
Blue fire can be obtained in the form of a Blue Fire Jar by using an Empty Jar on blue fire.

Usage[edit]
Blue fire can be placed using a Blue Fire Jar, leaving an Empty Jar in the players hand.
Other than being an annoyance and possibly a prank utility, blue fire has no uses by itself. It can not be used to inflict damage for use cases such as mob farms or combat like normal Template:MC can.

Trivia[edit]
As part of the 1,16 Template:MC, Mojang added their own version of blue fire to the base game known as Template:MC, this subsequently resulted in the removal of blue fire in later versions.

content:
Body Temperature is arguably the most prominent feature in Tough As Nails. Your body temperature is controlled by many different things, from the biome temperature, to the time of day, and more.
Below is a full list of things that can affect your body temperature:

Biome Temperature
Hot/Cold Source Blocks
Heating/Cooling Coils
Sprinting
Armor
Seasons
Time of Day
Weather
Wetness
Your body temperature is displayed by the orb in the middle of the HUD, between health and hunger. The color shifts from blue, to gray, to orange, depending on the temperature, and an up/down arrow animation will appear whenever the temperature changes. At the far ends of the temperature scale, the icon will change to a snowflake/flame, letting you know that you are close to hypothermia/hyperthermia.
There are a variety of ways to control your body temperature so that you don't get hypothermia/hyperthermia. For getting warm, the easiest way is to make a campfire. It's good for early-game survival, and requires very little resources. For cooling off, swimming in water is a great, easy way to keep cool.
Other ways to control your body temperature include armor, where wool armor can warm you up, and jelled slime armor can cool you off, heating & cooling coils, which are ideal for houses, potions of cold/heat resistance, and various other blocks that will warm you up/cool you off.
Keep in mind, your body temperature does not change instantly. It takes a while for it to change, and various things control the rate at which it changes, including your health level, wetness, biome humidity, and more. To monitor the environment temperature (The temperature that your body temperature works to change to), you can craft a thermometer.

The Bog biome is a flat, swampy land that is based on the real life Cranberry Bog. Bushes and maple scrub dominate the landscape, and reeds spawn in the water.

Contents

1 Description 

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival


2 Trivia 
3 Gallery



Description [edit]
Like most other swamps bog can be separated into two parts: the submerged part and the land. The land is flat (like most other swamps). The biome is made of reddish-orange grass.
The water here can be more than five blocks deep. The pond floor consists primarily of mud, although there are some portions of dirt and clay. Only Watergrass grows in the water.

Vegetation[edit]
A variety of plants are generated here, such as Sweet Berry Bushes, regular Bushes and Toadstools, but almost no flowers spawn here, apart from Dandelions and Poppies. Wheat Grass and Shrubs spawn, along single blocks of Oak Leaves. Birch and Dark Oak trees spawn sporadically.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Slimes spawn above ground at night, alongside the standard hostile mobs. Sheep, Pigs, and other passive mobs will spawn here.

Survival[edit]
Survival in this biome is average. With little quantities of wood, and the ability to obtain seeds from grass makes this biome survivable. When building shelters in water, players are safe from mobs because they cannot spawn on water.

Trivia [edit]
Bog, in real life, has mud that accumulates peat deposit of dead plant material, often mosses, and in most cases, Sphagnum moss (which is commonly known as "peat moss"). There are several types of peatlands, but this mod corresponds only to the trembling bogs. 
In previous versions of the mod, the bog has less land and are much more in flux and is less livable.
The old biome ID for Bogs are 176.
Bog was originally the name for Sludgepit when the mod was released.
The revamped Bog in 1.13.2 is based on the Cranberry Bog, as mentioned above.

  A Bone Segment.
Bone Segments are mined blocks that can be acquired from the Boneyard biome in the Nether. They can be small, medium or large and MUST be mined with a pickaxe.

Usage[edit]
All the bone segments are used in the creation of the Altar Frame. The Large Bone Segments are used in the crafting of the base altar, along with five Obsidian. The small and medium are also used, but only to form the altar.

The Boneyard is a Nether biome featuring backbone-like structures made from Bone Segments that jut from the ground and ceiling.

Versions[edit]
As of early April, 2016, Nether Biomes have not be re-added to 1.9 and 1.8.9 BoP, though the programmers are planning to bring them back. Boneyard was re-added in very early versions of 1.11.2, adding desert fossils. Later, it got removed again on build 2189.

Bramble is a plant that generates in Ominous Woods and Undergrowth biomes. It damages the player when standing on or next to its thorns. They also generate with Oak Leaves. They serve no practical purpose for defense as they only damage players and can be broken somewhat quickly, especially with an axe.

History[edit]
Bramble thorns were added in 1.12.2 as a Corrupted Sands biome exclusive. In 1.13.2 it was changed to generate in the Ominous Woods and Undergrowth biomes as the Corrupted Sands biome was removed.

content:
Bug Habitats are used to keep caught Butterflies and Dragonflies in. If you have an empty bug habitat in your inventory and use a Bug Net to catch an insect, it will automatically be placed in the habitat.
You can release insects from the habitat by right-clicking while holding it.
You cannot place this item on the ground.

summary:

Bug nets also lose durability with each catch.

title: Butterfly
summary:
Butterflies are a Passive Mob. They drop nothing upon death. Upon 1.10.2 update, butterflies are now identified as an Aggresive Mob and killing one will count to give the player the Monster Hunter achievement.
This mob has since been moved from Biomes O Plenty to the mod Familiar Fauna,a mod created...
content:
Butterflies are a Passive Mob. They drop nothing upon death. Upon 1.10.2 update, butterflies are now identified as an Aggresive Mob and killing one will count to give the player the Monster Hunter achievement.
This mob has since been moved from Biomes O' Plenty to the mod Familiar Fauna,a mod created by the same development team.
They inflict no damage but can occasionally bump into the player, pushing them slightly. Iron Golems also attacks them. They can be trapped using an Empty Jar which will then turn into a Butterfly Jar. Using (left clicking) a Butterfly Jar will release the Butterfly.
Butterflies will despawn once the player has reached enough distance for the chunks to unload. This can be prevented by using a Name Tag on the Butterfly.

Description[edit]
The Canyon biome is a fairly survivable biome to live in at the midway point. It contains hardened dirt and grass relative to the vanilla Plains biome, lava pools strewn across the surface, and virtually unscalable mountains and cliffs that jut far beyond the cloud level. Pine trees spawn here (those generating on the side of cliffs can extend much higher than normally), and impressive buildings can be made on the side of the mountains. Mobs do spawn here, sometimes even in the daytime because of outcrops from the large mountains. A bottleneck is usually the entrance, strewn with Coal Ore.
There is a sub-biome called Canyon Ravine, which generates at the edges of the Canyon biome.
The Canyon biome was removed in the 1.8.9 version of BoP, as well as Canyon Ravine.

Celestial Crystal is a glowstone-like block found in the End on the underside of the floating islands, or in singluar groups on the very tops of the islands. When broken it drops four Celestial Crystal Shards which can be re-combined, similar to glowstone dust.



Old[edit]


The shards were once found in the Promised Land before it was removed, and they were light blue rather than purple. The shards were also used to make ambrosia and the old ID was 1963.
Five were needed to create a Celestial Lens, required to make a Sacrificial Focus, both of which are now removed.

Cherry Blossom Groves were forests made up of white and pink Cherry Trees. The trees are reasonably spaced to create glades in this biome, and lots of flowers dot the landscape, such as pink daffodils, lilacs, peonies, and lilies of the valley. Flowering oak bushes and clovers also dot the forest. The normal range of passive mobs, such as Sheep, spawn here. There are a total of two variants in the biome family. Survival in this biome is quite easy with a reliable supply of trees and passive mobs. Each Cherry Tree gives a lot of wood due to the large size and branches. However, getting lost in this pink and white maze is very easy, and you will need to mark your exploration paths. There are oak trees that occasionally grow fruit so if you are running low on food you can harvest a few while waiting for a reliable source of food. Overall, this is a great biome for survival beginners. Cherry Wood is a great building material for shelter and tools. It is a very pretty red that looks different from most other logs, and creates very deep red planks. The many flowers around the biome can be crafted into dyes, which can be used to dye sheep and obtain colored wool.

Contents

1 Bamboo Grove
2 Trivia
3 History
4 Gallery



Bamboo Grove[edit]
Bamboo Groves are a sub-biome of Cherry Blossom Groves that contain lots of bamboo and less cherry trees. They are slightly rarer than the regular biome.

Trivia[edit]
Cherry Blossom trees cannot be lit on fire with a flint and steel in versions earlier than 1.8 due to a bug.
The old ID for this biome before 1.8 was 181.
The old ID for this biome in 1.7.10 was 49.
History[edit]
Cherry Blossom Grove, alongside Bamboo Grove, were removed in 1.20 because the Cherry Grove was added in vanilla Minecraft.

Clovers are plants that appear like a four-leaf clover in the Grassland biome and its Clover Patch variant, as well as the Cherry Blossom Grove, Bamboo Grove and Mystic Grove.  Breaking Clover by hand drops nothing, while using Shears on a Clover drops itself.  Using Bone Meal on a Clover gives a chance for that plant to grow into four Huge Clover Petals arranged to resemble a much larger clover.  This plant does not appear to be a renewable resource.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.



Per the official Mojang Brand Guidelines, works that contain Minecraft assets may be used freely on this Wiki.If this work contains elements added by Biomes O' Plenty, the Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 License also applies (forum post).


Biomes O' Plenty has one command named /biomesoplenty; this has been added since 1.8 and remained until 1.16.1.

Contents

1 /biomesoplenty

1.1 tpbiome instructions
1.2 biomename instructions
1.3 





/biomesoplenty[edit]
/biomesoplenty, or /bop for short, is used for three things:

Teleporting to biomes
Finding the ID for biomes
Removing all types of certain blocks from a given chunk radius
tpbiome instructions[edit]
tpbiome is used to teleport to biomes, to use it you type, for example:
/bop tpbiome 50
This will teleport you to a Cherry Blossom Grove biome
In place of 50, type a number between 40 and 102 to find a biomes o'plenty biome. Numbers 0-39 are all vanilla biomes.
If it says "Could Not Find Biome [biomename]!" as an error message in chat, that means that there is none of the biome you want within 10,000 blocks of you. If it says "Could Not Find Biome Undefined!", then that means the biome doesn't exist.
In 1.8, you used to be able to type the biome's name instead, but since 1.9 it is now the biome's ID. 
In 1.13.2 and higher, this has changed to a full ID rather than a number ID, since number IDs and data values got removed due to 1.13's flattening, such as:
/bop tpbiome biomesoplenty:bayou
The /biomesoplenty command was removed in 1.16.1 due to vanilla adding the /locatebiome command, but thankfully, that command can work on BOP biomes as well.
Here's an example how to teleport to any BOP biome using /locatebiome:
/locatebiome biomesoplenty:silkglade
This will give the coordinates in the chat. Open the chat and click on the coordinates, and press Enter. This will teleport you to the Silkglades.

Note: NOT all BiomesOPlenty biomes are present in the command

biomename instructions[edit]
biomename is used to find the name of each biome ID.
/bop *biomename* 50
In this example, upon typing it, a message will come up in chat of the name of the biome using biome id 48 (Cherry Blossom Grove). The normal biomes appear first in alphabetical order, and then subbiomes appear, and at the end, oceanic biomes. 40 is Gravel Beach


[edit]

NOTE: This wiki is not supported or endorsed by the developers! Information found here may be inaccurate/outdated, and should not be used as reference for issues, bug reports, or any other requests to the developers!
This page documents the various functions of the Biomes O' Plenty configuration files as of BOP version 2.1.0 and later. The files are listed in alphabetic or zip files.

Contents

1 Current
2 world.json
3 Biome_ids.JSON
4 gameplay.cfg
5 misc.cfg
6 Before 1.12

6.1 biomegen.cfg
6.2 biomeweights.cfg
6.3 ids.cfg
6.4 main.cfg
6.5 misc.cfg
6.6 terraingen.cfg


7 Structures

7.1 s
7.2 strongholds


8 Resetting the config



Current[edit]
All the BOP configuration files can be found within %appdata%\.minecraft\config\biomesoplenty\ on Windows. In all the configuration files, true and false correspond to on and off, respectively. Since 1.8, most files on the config file have been removed because of the Customize world setting.
To change customization options on a server, add the follow string to generator-settings in server.properties:

{
  "landScheme": "vanilla",
  "tempScheme": "medium_zones",
  "rainScheme": "medium_zones",
  "biomeSize": "medium",
  "amplitude": 1,
  "generateBopOre": true,
  "generateBopSoils": true,
  "generateBopTrees": true,
  "generateBopGrasses": true,
  "generateBopFoliage": true,
  "generateBopFlowers": true,
  "generateBopPlants": true,
  "generateBopWaterPlants": true,
  "generateBopMushrooms": true,
  "generateRockFormations": true,
  "generatePoisonIvy": false,
  "generateFlax": true,
  "generateBerryBushes": true,
  "generateThorns": true,
  "generateQuicksand": true,
  "generateLiquidPoison": true,
  "generateHotSprings": true,
  "generateNetherHives": true,
  "generateNetherPlants": true,
  "generateEndFeatures": true
}
If you are using other vanilla generator settings, add them inside of the braces and separate each option with a comma.
world.json[edit]
Alternatively, you can change the server configuration by creating a world.json file within the config/biomesoplenty folder. In this file, copy the following into it:

{
  "landScheme": "archipelago",
  "tempScheme": "medium_zones",
  "rainScheme": "medium_zones",
  "biomeSize": "medium",
  "amplitude": 1,
  "generateBopOre": true,
  "generateBopSoils": true,
  "generateBopTrees": true,
  "generateBopGrasses": true,
  "generateBopFoliage": true,
  "generateBopFlowers": true,
  "generateBopPlants": true,
  "generateBopWaterPlants": true,
  "generateBopMushrooms": true,
  "generateRockFormations": true,
  "generatePoisonIvy": true,
  "generateBerryBushes": true,
  "generateThorns": true,
  "generateQuicksand": true,
  "generateLiquidPoison": true,
  "generateHotSprings": true,
  "generateNetherHives": true,
  "generateEndFeatures": true,
  "mainNoiseScaleX": 80,
  "mainNoiseScaleY": 160,
  "mainNoiseScaleZ": 80,
  "coordinateScale": 684.412,
  "heightScale": 684.412,
  "upperLimitScale": 512,
  "lowerLimitScale": 512
}

Changing the values in this file will change the customization option on the server. These settings are up-to-date as of 1.12.2.

Biome_ids.JSON[edit]
This file contains the biome IDs for each biome, but they are in random order. Set a biome ID to -1 disabled when generating a biome from version 3.0.0.1632 or later.

gameplay.cfg[edit]
This file only contains an option for using shears when collecting BOP flowers.

misc.cfg[edit]
This file contains options for changing the Biomes O'Plenty and Default settings under the world generation type, and options for the panorama on the Minecraft menu and bucket texture settings.

Before 1.12[edit]
All the BOP configuration can be found within %appdata%\.minecraft\config\biomesoplenty\ on Windows. In all the configuration files, true and false correspond to on and off, respectively.

biomegen.cfg[edit]
This file controls which BOP biomes spawn. Changing the true to false for the biomes listed under "overworld biomes to generate" will remove that biome and any of its sub-biomes from the world generation. All sub-biomes are listed under "overworld (sub) biomes to generate" and can be individually disabled from there.
Vanilla biomes cannot be disabled, but under "vanilla biomes to override", the small changes that BOP does to specific vanilla biomes can be toggled either true (on) or false (off). Everything should be set to true by default in this file.

biomeweights.cfg[edit]
This file controls the weighting of all BOP biomes. You can make adjustments to how often specific BOP biomes spawn by increasing or decreasing the number at the end of each line corresponding to a specific biome. Vanilla biomes are not listed.

ids.cfg[edit]
This file controls which numerical IDs are assigned to which biomes. The numerical biome IDs range from 0 to 255. If you have other mods installed that add biomes to Minecraft, it would be a good idea to check and ensure that the IDs specified in ids.cfg do not collide with other added biomes. Vanilla biomes are not listed in this file.

main.cfg[edit]
This file allows you to toggle debug mode, which isn't needed by most users. By default, it is set to false.

misc.cfg[edit]
This file controls other elements that do not fit in the other configuration files. Custom sky colors and the added haze that some biomes have can be toggled in this file, along with some options that pertain to the main Minecraft menu.

terraingen.cfg[edit]
The SMES generated can be toggled on the line that contains I:"Biome Size". 4 is the default biome size; 6 is equivalent to the vanilla large biomes generation option. The input on this line can range from 1 to 8.
The generation of BOP ores can also be controlled using true or false. By default, all are set to true.

Structures[edit]
The structures folder can be found in the main BOP config folder, biomesoplenty. It should contain two config files. Note that this does not appear in 1.8.

s[edit]
This file specifies which biomes strongholds can spawn in. By default, all lines should be set to true.

strongholds[edit]
This file specifies which biomes strongholds can spawn in. Avoid messing with this file, as some biomes will not look well with strongholds.

Resetting the config[edit]
If you wish to reset a config file to its default state, simply delete it. Upon running the game, any missing config files will generate with their default settings. Alternatively, deleting the entire biomesoplenty folder from the config folder will regenerate all the configuration files with default settings when you next run Minecraft with BOP loaded.

Coniferous Forests are biomes that feature tall Fir Trees, as well as toadstools, berry bushes, ferns and grass, and the occasional dandelions, cornflowers, poppies and oxeye daisies. Some passive mobs can spawn in the biome, such as sheep. This biome is easy to survive in, though the tall trees may provide darkness for hostile mobs to spawn. There are a total of 4 biomes in the biome family.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Fir Clearing
1.2 Snowy Coniferous Forest
1.3 Snowy Fir Clearing


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Fir Clearing[edit]
Fir Clearings are variants which instead feature smaller and way fewer trees.

Snowy Coniferous Forest[edit]
Snowy Coniferous Forests are variants that are covered in snow, and less grass and ferns spawn here. Violets spawn here as well.

Snowy Fir Clearing[edit]
Snowy Fir Clearings are variants similar to the Fir Clearing but with less grass, ferns, and violets do spawn here.

Trivia[edit]
The old Biome ID before 1.8 was 182.
Coniferous forests are mainly found in the northern parts of the world like Russia, Sweden and Finland.
The regular Coniferous Forest is Forstride's favorite biome.

Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in 4 variants: pink, orange, blue and glowing. It can be found in coral reefs and was removed from the mod in Minecraft 1.13 Template:MC with the addition of Vanilla's version of Template:MC.

Breaking[edit]
Coral can be mined instantly with an empty hand or item/tool and it will always drop itself.

Natural Generation[edit]
All coral variants generate densely in coral reefs.

Other than ambience and decoration, Coral has no use.

Minecraft 1.13 - Coral was removed due to Mojang introducing coral to the base game.

Corrupted Sands is a biome found in the Nether. It is made of large areas of soul sand with frequent Thorns, Bramble and Dead Grass. Quicksand pools also spawn and can obstruct paths in Nether Fortresses.

Contents

1 History
2 Gallery

2.1 Newer
2.2 Older





History[edit]
The Corrupted Sands Biome was originally just a flat biome full of soul sand. Phantoms originally spawned here before their removal. In 1.11.2 it was redesigned to have much better variation and much more Thorns, making it more detailed. In 1.12.2, Bramble thorns were added. In 1.13.2, it was removed.

The Crag is a mountainous biome with dizzying peaks and often a few floating islands.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
The terrain here consists of Cobblestone, Stone, Gravel, and Overgrown Stone. The peaks can get as high as the world's sky limit.

Vegetation[edit]
Largely absent.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Also largely absent. Except hostile mobs.

Survival[edit]
Surviving in the crags can be difficult since only Damp Grass grows here. Your only food source would be rotten flesh and rarely carrots and potatoes from zombies and your only source of wood occurring in this biome would be from the lucky find of an abandoned mineshaft. Other things such as seeds, saplings and passive mobs would have to be transported here. If you aren't careful you may fall and if you do, you'll most likely die. Some places in the crags would be brilliant places to build grand fortresses. It's not the best biome to start off in because of these factors.

History[edit]
Water used to be coloured dark dull blue until 1.11.2 where the biome was redesigned. Crag Roc been removed too.

title: Crop Fertility
summary:
Crop Fertility is a key feature in Serene Seasons.
Throughout the seasons, the types of crops you can grow will change. Crops can be set to grow in any of the temperate seasons, and in biomes affected by tropical seasons, only Summer crops will be in season. Likewise, biomes that always receive snow...
content:
Crop Fertility is a key feature in Serene Seasons.
Throughout the seasons, the types of crops you can grow will change. Crops can be set to grow in any of the temperate seasons, and in biomes affected by tropical seasons, only Summer crops will be in season. Likewise, biomes that always receive snow will only be able to grow Winter crops.
You can see which season(s) a crop is fertile in the tooltip that appears when you hover over the seeds for the crop, or in some cases, the crop itself.
When a crop is in season, it will grow as it normally does, and you'll be able to use bonemeal to grow it faster like normal. When a crop is out of season, it will grow very slowly, and will require more bonemeal than usual to increase its growth stage. To grow out of season crops efficiently, you have three options:
1. Placing glass/stained glass blocks within 16 blocks above crops to grow out of season crops above ground.
2. Using bees. Bees will pollinate crops regardless of whether they're in season or not.
3. Growing out of season crops underground, as long as they're below a certain Y level (48 by default) and not exposed to the sky.

A White Dandelion is a white flower generally found in Fungi Forest, Timber, Prairie, and other such biomes. It can be used as a decorative block, or crafted into Light Gray Dye. It is also possible to blow the dandelion as you could in real life; to do this just right-click while holding the dandelion in your hand.

Dart
	
		
		
	
	

	

		Type
	Ammo

		Renewable
	No

		Stackable
	Yes



Darts are projectile ammunition, similar to arrows. They can be shot out of a Dart Blower or a Dispenser.
Darts deal a  of damage and break upon impact, but they can be shot without charging to make up for their disadvantage.

Removal[edit]
Darts and Dart Blowers were removed in later versions of BOP for Minecraft 1.9. They were probably removed because of them not fitting Biomes O' Plenty's style. They might be moved to Glitchfiend's other mods, such as the survival mods.

Crafting[edit]
One Thorn, River Cane and a Feather can be used to craft four darts, similar to the arrow recipe.

Using poison and a Dart can be turned into a Poison Dart.


Trivia[edit]
The old item ID is 21269/0.

Dead Forests are bleak, brown landscapes with dead trees, oak trees, and spruce trees scattered along the landscape. No flowers spawn here, and grass is sparse. On the dead trees, you'll find dead branches. Despite what you may think, survival is somewhat easy here due to the minimal but manageable supply of wood and other resources, though food may be a challenge to obtain due to the fact that no animals spawn here.

Wooded Wasteland
Dead Grass is a type of grass that can be found in the Wasteland biome. It yields nothing when broken by hand, but can be harvested with shears.
Like other BOP grasses, and vanilla grass, Dead Grass has not only X and Z axis offsets, but Y axis offsets, making the height of the plant dependant on where the grass is placed. Every seed has an unique pattern.

The Dead Swamp, formerly known as Mire, is a biome filled with dark, muddy ponds and sparse, dead trees.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival


2 Trivia
3 History
4 Gallery



Description[edit]
This biome features large areas of Loamy Grass and Mud, with frequent, muddy ponds. The water has a dark, slightly green color. Unlike most swamp biomes, there is no Clay.

Vegetation[edit]
Dead Trees appear somewhat sparsely, and River Cane and Reeds are common around the water. Grass and Koru can also be found.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
No passive mobs spawn in this biome. Besides villagers in their villages.

Survival[edit]
For new players, it's hard to survive. There are almost no animals walking around and very hard to escape because of large biome fields.

Trivia[edit]
The old biome ID before 1.8 was 187.
History[edit]
It was removed in 1.16.5

title: Dead Tree
summary: Dead Trees are dull looking trees, mostly lacking leaves. They can be found in the Dead Forest, Old Growth Dead Forest, Muskeg, Ominous Woods, Wasteland, and Tundra biomes. Unique branches can sometimes be found on the tree called Dead Branch. There are four shapes of the tree, the first shape being...
content:
Dead Trees are dull looking trees, mostly lacking leaves. They can be found in the Dead Forest, Old Growth Dead Forest, Muskeg, Ominous Woods, Wasteland, and Tundra biomes. Unique branches can sometimes be found on the tree called Dead Branch. There are four shapes of the tree, the first shape being a tall log with very few to no leaves and some dead branches found in almost all the dead tree biomes except the Tundra and can be grown via sapling, the second shape is a standard oak tree shape that can be grown via sapling and found in the Dead Forest and Old Growth Dead Forest, the third is a unique tree shape with log coming out forming branch shapes and a fair amount of leaves found in all dead tree biomes except the Tundra and Muskeg, the last shape is a tiny tree with about five leaves only found in the Tundra. The color of the wood is a bleak gray, and the texture of the door and trapdoors look like they've been broken.

The Deadlands biome is an ash-covered wasteland with blood-red water, smoldering grass blocks, lava pools and open pits nearly 40 blocks deep.
The entire biome is covered in ash blocks, even underwater, with scattered smoldering grass blocks on the land.
Surviving in the Deadlands is difficult because there is no dirt, no wood and no passive mobs. The threat of death by fire and lava is always present. But the red-as-blood water wants to eat you ( >:-D ) Thirst effect is applied here also.
As of version 1.2.1, the Deadlands are disabled by default. The mod developer stated on Reddit that he plans to remove the biome in the version of the mod that updates to Minecraft 1.7. (reference link)

The Deciduous Forest biome has tall oak trees with birch and oak shrubs on the ground. Animals, mainly sheep, spawn in this biome, along with plenty of grass and berry bushes. Flax can also be found in this biome.
This biome was removed in BOP 1.8.9.

Survivability[edit]
Surviving here is very easy, as wood and food are quite plentiful. Like all forest biomes, dark areas can provide refuge for hostile mobs during the day, so watch out.

content:
Deer used to be passive mobs that would generally spawn in temperate forest biomes, as well as some colder biomes. They could randomly spawn as either a doe (Female) or buck (Male), and could sometimes appear naturally in their baby form.
Deer were also very skittish, and would run away from nearby players.
When killed, mature deer dropped Venison, a meat that could be eaten raw, or cooked to restore additional hunger.
This was a familiar fauna feature, but familiar fauna was discontinued.

Desert Grass is a short grass that can only be placed on regular sand, red sand, orange sand, white sand, and black sand. It is found in Scrublands, Wooded Scrublands, Wastelands, Wooded Wastelands, Cold Deserts, and Lush Deserts. It can be composted, and has a 50% chance to gain matter.

Like other BOP grasses, and vanilla grass, Desert Grass has not only X and Z axis offsets, but Y axis offsets, making the height of the plant dependant on where the grass is placed. Every seed has an unique pattern.
