This page describes the variations of dirt added by the Biomes O' Plenty mod. To learn more about dirt in general please see Template:MC.
Biomes O' Plenty adds three new variations of Template:MC, known as Loamy Dirt, Sandy Dirt, and Silty Dirt.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Natural Generation

1.1.1 Loamy Dirt
1.1.2 Sandy Dirt
1.1.3 Silty Dirt




2 Usage
3 History



Obtaining[edit]
Just like normal Template:MC, it can be mined and obtained with any tool, but a Template:MC is fastest.

Natural Generation[edit]
Biomes O' Plenty's dirt variations replace several parts of the surface that would usually be covered with regular Template:MC depending on the biome.

Loamy Dirt[edit]
Loamy dirt is mostly found in wet biomes, such as Template:MC, and the Fen biome.

Sandy Dirt[edit]
Sandy dirt is found mostly in dry and hot biomes such as the Xeric Shrubland.

Silty Dirt[edit]
Silty dirt can be found in temperate biomes such as in the Cherry Blossom Grove or Lavender Fields.

Usage[edit]
All dirt variations and their derivatives can be used in the same way, they only differ in appearance. They can be used as farmland, to grow saplings, sugarcane, mushrooms, etc. and behaves just like how Template:MC does in the base game.

History[edit]


1.7.10

 Loamy Dirt was added to world generation, Sandy and Silty dirt were also added but did not naturally generate and were unobtainable in survival.


1.8

  Sandy and Silty Dirt were added to world generation.


1.13.2

 All added dirt variations and their derivatives were removed from the mod.

Dragonflies are ambient mobs that spawn in wet, temperate biomes. They appear in a variety of colors, and fly around in the air.
This mob has since been moved from Biomes O' Plenty to the mod Familiar Fauna,a mod created by the same development team.
Dragonflies can be caught using Bug Nets and Bug Habitats. If you have an empty Bug Habitat in your inventory, the dragonfly will automatically be placed in it when caught.
Additionally, dragonflies named using Name Tags will retain their name even when caught and placed in a Bug Habitat. The name will stay if you release them as well.

The Dryland  is a hot, dry biome scattered with Pine Trees, Oak Trees, and smaller brush-like oak trees. The ground is covered with tons of grass, bushes, dead bushes, and tiny cacti. Tons of bone block structures also spawn here. The sky is slightly purple in this biome. This biome should be fairly easy to survive in, due to the abundance of wood, and that passive mobs such as sheep, cows and chickens can spawn here.

History[edit]


1.6.2

The Brushland biome is added. The biome contains small trees that are made of jungle logs and oak leaves. It grows grass, wheat grass, shrubs, alliums, red mushrooms, and thorns. The biome also has patches of quicksand and pools of water.


1.8

Reeds now spawn in the pools of water.


1.8.9

Sandy Grass, and Sandy Dirt is replaced for regular grass and dirt blocks. Small trees made of jungle logs and oak leaves no longer spawn. Unique Acacia and Ebony Trees spawn in the biome. Alliums no longer grow here. Short Grass and Medium Grass now grow in the biome. Patches of quicksand are more pool looking.


1.9

Tiny Jungle Trees spawn and sometimes contain cocoa beans.


1.12.2

Shrubs no longer grow in the biome.


1.13.2

Sandy Grass/Dirt, Quicksand, Thorns, Short Grass, Medium Grass, Ebony Trees, Jungle Trees, and pools of water no longer spawn in this biome. Acacia Trees are much shorter and Dead Trees now spawn. Desert Grass, Dead Grass, Tiny Cacti, and Bushes now grow here. Patches of sand spawn again and are larger. Patches of sand also contain Dune Grass, Cacti, and Dead Bushes.

Trivia[edit]
If Serene Seasons is installed, the foliage in the biome will turn blue because of the way the tinting works in the mod.
This biome used to be called Brushland, but it was renamed to Dryland in 1.16.3.
Older versions of this biome used to have Ebony trees instead of oak trees.

The Dune Beach biome is a biome similar to that of a beach, but it is covered in Dune Grass and Sea Oats. Sandstone generates under the biome, like normal beaches. No trees generate here. It does not have a specific temperature that it generates in, however it will always spawn near oceans.
WARNING: THE FOLLOWING CONTENT IS OUTDATED
The Dunes biome is a dynamic desert-like biome. It has a great deal of sandy hills, mountains and plateaus covered sparsely with dune grass, bromeliads and many small acacia trees among the arid highlands. Dunes often appear in other vanilla type deserts. Survival here is not the easiest. With a great abundance of sandstone, it also lacks trees, which are important for crafting wooden tools which can contribute to mining. 

History[edit]


1.3.2

Dunes were added to the mod.


1.7.2

The Dunes biome was removed.


1.17.1

The Dunes biome was re-added, with Dune Grass and Sea Oats, being a sub-biome of Template:MC.


1.18.2

Dunes was renamed to Dune Beach, and now generates as a beach biome instead.

Dune Grass is a type of grass that can be placed on sandy blocks. It generates naturally in the Dune Beach and Lush Desert biomes. It can be composted, and has a 50% chance to gain matter.

Like other BOP grasses, and vanilla grass, Dune Grass has not only X and Z axis offsets, but Y axis offsets, making the height of the plant dependant on where the grass is placed. Every seed has an unique pattern.

Empty honeycomb block is a block found in hives generated in the Nether. The block can be collected with a tool that has silk touch on it. Axes break this block the quickest.Breaking the block will cause a Wasp to spawn

Uses[edit]
It can be used as a furnace fuel and smelts 1 1/2 items. It can also be placed as a decoration block.

content:
Empyreal Trees are found in the End Wilds biome. They grow in an unusual, twisting form. The trees can sometimes have a Shroomlight inside of them or a water drop shape levitating on the top of the tree. These trees can grow pretty tall, especially if the top part of the tree has its levitating bush.
The leaves of the tree are a boney-white color, and the bark of the logs are a light gray color. Planks, stripped log, etc. are all purple. The door and trapdoor are a similar texture to the bark of the tree but in a purple color with black hinges.

Resources[edit]
Logs: Empyreal Logs
Leaves: Empyreal Leaves

Other: Sometimes Shroomlight

The End Corruption is an End biome that resembles the game being corrupted. Endermen do not spawn, and the terrain features random missing texture pits with anomalies above them, small pillars of Obsidian, broken and glitchy trees, pools of liquid and plants. The ground also appears to be glitchy, with End Stone having lines on the sides. Binary number particles can be found in the air.

The End Reef is an End biome that is a dead coral reef. The ground features White Sand with small water patches surrounded by dead coral and White Sandstone pillars. Barnacles also appear both on the ground and on the walls. Wispjelly jellyfish is found in the air, along with bubble particles.

Trivia[edit]
According to Forstride, Wispjelly forms when the water evaporates in the End.[1]

The End Wilds is an End biome that has lots of plant growth and Empyreal Trees. Similar to the Crimson and Warped Forests, regular End Stone is replaced with Algal End Stone. The plants found in the biome are Enderphyte, Endbloom, and Lumaloop. Shroomlights from the Empyreal Trees and Lumaloop light up the biome. Goldish-brown particles are also seen in the air.

Trivia[edit]
End Wilds is based on the biome of the same name from Minecraft Dungeons.

Ender Amethyst is a biome-specific gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History
5 Trivia



Generation[edit]
Ender Amethyst Ore is only obtainable in the outer islands.

Obtaining[edit]
A Diamond Pickaxe is required to mine Ender Amethyst Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Amethyst drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted diamond pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Ender Amethyst Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Amethyst can be crafted into a Block of Amethyst for storage, decoration or showing off your riches. These stack to 64. It is a key ingredient in the Biome Finder.

Crafting recipes:[edit]


Name

Ingredients

Crafting Recipe

Description


Block of Amethyst

Ender Amethyst

  

Decorative block made of Ender Amethyst gems. It drops the prefix "Ender" in this form.


Biome Finder

Ender Amethyst, Terrestrial Artifact

  

A crafting component used in the Biome Finder, Enderporter, and Wanderer Music Disc

History[edit]
Before 1.7.2, Amethyst was found in the Promised Land. However after the Promised Land was removed, it was useless, until 1.9.4 where it was re-added to The End along with Biome Essence Ore and Celestial Crystals.
It was also a piece required for several removed items or armor and tools. And completely removed in 1.13.2 and higher.


Trivia[edit]
In real life, amethyst is the name of purple quartz.
In real life, diamond is stronger than Amethyst. It is only a 7 on the Mohs hardness scale, while diamonds are ten—the highest value of any mineral. However, some claim that lonsdaleite is even harder.
The old ID for Amethyst before 1.8 was 21266/2.

This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
Enderporter
	
		
		
	
	

	Enderporter



An Enderporter is a teleportation device that sends the player within several hundred blocks of spawn and has 9 uses.
It spawns the player at height 254.380, higher than any block in the game.
The player is spawned with 4 seconds of Night Vision, 4 seconds of Blindness, 9 seconds of Resistance and 9 seconds of Regeneration IV. These buffs keep the player from seeing where they will land, but keep them from dying upon impact as it only take 5 seconds to fall from 254 to 0, leaving the player with an additional 4 seconds of Resistance and Regeneration IV. 

Crafting[edit]
Before Build 1.9.4-4.1.0.2057, Crafting an Enderporter required 4 Ghastly Souls, 4 Eye of Enders, and a single Amethyst. Now it requires 5 Amethyst and 4 Ender Eyes.

The Eucalyptus Forest is a biome featuring tall trees, based on areas of Australian forest.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
The Eucalyptus Forest is a forest/jungle biome featuring tall, thin trees made from eucalyptus wood and leaves. Leaf blocks make up a lot of brush on the ground. The overall terrain is flat, with occasional hills. In versions prior to 1.8 this biome's ID is 56.

Vegetation[edit]
Large Eucalyptus Trees grow in this biome, featuring colourful wood. The ground is littered with oak shrubs. Melon and Pumpkin Blocks, Poppies, Dandelions, and Rafflesia will spawn. This biome will also spawn various water lilies.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Parrots spawn in this biome. Villagers cannot spawn in this biome, although they could in earlier versions. Jungle Temples may also spawn in this biome

Survival[edit]
The abundance of trees, tall grass, and the presence of a few scattered passive mobs provide for relatively easy survivability in this biome. Melons provide an immediate crop and food source. It should be noted that the height of Eucalyptus Trees can make them difficult to harvest.

History[edit]
It was added in 1.7.10, where trees used Jungle Wood because there was no Eucalyptus Wood added in 1.7.10, and had a white fog. In 1.8, Eucalyptus Wood was added and the white fog was removed. It is removed in 1.13.2 and upwards.

Eyebulb is a block found in the Visceral Heap biome. It's two blocks tall and has four texture variants. Fen was a swampy biome with reeds and cattails, with muddy pools and short evergreen trees.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Terrain
1.2 Vegetation

1.2.1 Mobs & NPCs




2 Survival

2.1 Exploring


3 History
4 Gallery



Description[edit]
A swampy forest with Mud, Cattails, Reeds, and somewhat short trees.
This biome can also have name "Dying forest"

Terrain[edit]
Terrain is flat rarely with hills.

Vegetation[edit]
This biome features Dark Oak Trees, Cattails, and Reeds. Lily pads can be found in the shallow pools scattered around the biome.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Slimes can be found above ground in the Fen. Passive mobs such as Cows and Sheep will spawn.

Survival[edit]
Survival is easy because there is lot of trees and cows and sheep spawn here.The dying trees can be farmed for persimmons, making a great early food source.

Exploring[edit]
Exploring is safe because there isn't anything that can hurt you, but mobs can hide under trees and in caves.

History[edit]
After BOP 2.0.0, Oak Trees changed to Dark Oak Trees and villages began to spawn in Fen. Villages no longer spawn in Fen biomes, according to the most recent config files, but you can enable them by editing config file.

	Peridot (Note: Gemstones are a feature exclusive to versions 1.12 and below.)


Fields are pretty flatlands with teal-ish grass and lots of sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes, azure bluets, tulips, lilies of the valley, poppies, and dandelions. Sprouts and grass also cover lots of the ground. It is usually flat, and sparsely forested with small spruce trees, but oak bushes generate often in clusters here. Most passive mobs, such as cows and pigs, spawn here, as well as rarely, foxes. Occasionally, you will find a bee nest on a tree. Villages can spawn in this biome and they tend to feature spruce wood. This is by far one of the best places to live, with flat land for building and plenty of wood and passive mobs, it should be extremely easy to survive here.

Forested Field[edit]
The forested field is a variant-biome, and as its name suggests, is a forested version of the biome. It contains slightly less oak bushes and flowers.

History[edit]
In historic versions a removed flower, the White Dandelion, spawned here.
This biome used to be called Meadow, and its variant, Meadow Forest, but it was renamed to Field in 1.18 due to the addition of the vanilla Meadow biome.

Description[edit]
Similar to Grassland, Fields are dominated by Grass along with Poppies, and the limited number of trees makes survival difficult. It is challenging to build a shelter since trees are sparse. You can make a dugout if you want; that will be your shelter, but the main difficulty of the biome is there is little available wood. If you're lucky, you may find some mineshafts underground. Passive mobs spawn in this biome so food shouldn't be a problem.

Forested Field[edit]
There is one sub biome called the Forested Field, it contains sparse pine and oak.

title: Fir Tree
summary: Fir Trees are found in the Coniferous Forest, Fir Clearing, Auroral Garden, and the since removed Alps biome. Fir trees are fairly large, at around 50 blocks tall, and are a little bit taller than a 2x2 spruce tree. They can be grown with one sapling, or four saplings in a 2x2 grid, just like spruce...
content:
Fir Trees are found in the Coniferous Forest, Fir Clearing, Auroral Garden, and the since removed Alps biome. Fir trees are fairly large, at around 50 blocks tall, and are a little bit taller than a 2x2 spruce tree. They can be grown with one sapling, or four saplings in a 2x2 grid, just like spruce trees. On Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, fir leaves appear to be decorated with Christmas lights. They are very tall and can be used to get lots of wood. 
The Fir logs, planks, etc. are all a dull gray texture. The sapling is a retextured version of the spruce tree. The door and trap door has a chain connected to a ball instead of a doorknob. The tree itself (when grown with four saplings) starts in a 2x2 grid at the base but ends with one block at the top. It also has logs poking out from the trunk of the tree.

Crafting (1.14.4 and higher): signs

Flesh is a block found in the Visceral Heap biome.
Its loot drops were changed as of 1.13 from Chunks of Flesh to itself.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Natural Generation
1.2 Breaking
1.3 Blood


2 Usage
3 Gallery



Obtaining[edit]
Natural Generation[edit]
Flesh can be found in abundance within the Visceral Heap covering the biomes floor, walls, roof and features.
Porous Flesh was added in a more recent version of Biomes O' Plenty and generates in small patches within the Visceral Heap.

Breaking[edit]
With the removal of the Chunk of Flesh in 1.13, Flesh will always drop itself when broken by the player.Any tool can be used to break Flesh, and it will always drop its item, but an Template:MC is fastest.

Blood[edit]
Flowing blood will transform water source blocks it comes in contact with into flesh.

Usage[edit]
Other than decoration, Flesh by itself has no real uses.

Natural Generation[edit]
Flesh Tendons can only be found in the Visceral Heap.

Breaking[edit]
Flesh Tendons can only be obtained by using shears. They can be broken quickly with an axe but don't drop anything.

Placing[edit]
Flesh Tendons can only be placed under Flesh, and Porous Flesh.

Usage[edit]
Other than decoration, Flesh Tendons by themselves have no real uses.

Floodplains are tropical biomes similar to marshes, but with small brush-like oak trees generating. Their surface is littered with lots of grass, tall grass and oak bushes, and occasionally orange cosmos, dandelions and poppies. In the inundated portions of this biome, watergrass, seagrass, small dripleaves, lily pads, huge lily pads and waterlilies can be found frequently. Survival is not adequate, but it is okay, due to the prevalence of wood, but lack of food. However, you can get wheat by breaking the frequent grass that spawns here.
There are no sub-biomes.

Trivia[edit]
This biome used to be a sub-biome of the rainforest, though it will still generate near it.

Description[edit]
The ground is entirely covered with grass blocks, and a red, orange, white, or pink Tulip on almost every single block.

Vegetation[edit]
This biome has no other flora beyond Tulips and Grass.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs like Sheep, Cows, etc spawn here.

Survival[edit]
The Flower Field has no trees at all, so it isn't really a good biome for a first day. Pigs and Sheep spawn here though, providing meat and wool for beds. If you get saplings and plant them in the Flower Field, you can survive. But be careful, since there's no coverage from hostile mobs that spawn at night.

The Flower Island (Formerly the Garden Biome), is rolling hills covered with vibrant vegetation and Giant Flowers instead of trees. This is the only biome where Rosesters naturally spawn. As of 1.8, it is now an ocean sub-biome.

Description[edit]
The Biome is flattened hills, fluctuating between 70 and 80 at most heights. Instead of regular grass blocks the surface is comprised of Flowering Grass Blocks covered in shrubs, sprouts, high grass and patches of flowers like Roses, Dandelions,  Sunflowers, White Anemones and Blue Hydrangeas. Occasional oak shrubs spawn. Mobs such as the Rosester also spawned here. Sky color here is normal, aswell as the foliage color.
It was removed in 1.14.

Survival[edit]
Although it may seem like paradise, the lack of trees requires importing trees from elsewhere, ( being the mainland). Flattening the dense grass is also laborious. The ID before 1.8 was 195.

A Flowered Lily Pad is a type of lily pad found in Swampland and Tropical biomes.

Trivia[edit]
  In Minecraft 1.9.4, ever since Quicksand has been a liquid, Flowered Lily Pads have been unintentionally spawning in Quicksand Pools.
Whilst most other things with flowers have been named "Flowering" (Flowering Oak Tree, Flowering Grass Block), these were named "Flowered" instead.

Flowers are non-solid plants that are able to be pollinated and usually have vibrant colors along with a stem and leaves. They are primarily used for decoration, and can also be crafted into dyes. Small plants can also be potted, and crafted into Suspicious Stew for varying status effects, with the sole exception to both of these being Wildflowers. Any effects gained from Suspicious Stews crafted out of BOP flowers will last for only a negligible amount of time.
Flowers were added in the first versions of BOP, however many have been removed, changed or added since then.

Trivia[edit]
In the vanilla version of Minecraft, the Rose texture was the predecessor to the Poppy.
In earlier versions of Minecraft, a flower's hitbox was always in the center of the block it is on, no matter what position the flower is in. This was changed in later versions, but the Rose's hitbox is in the center of the block, instead of being where the flower is as a reference to old Minecraft.
In older versions of BOP, the Pink Daffodil was misspelled as "Pink Dafodil".
In very old versions of BOP, Orange Cosmos were originally called Orange Daisies, and had a different texture.
Since Blue Hydrangeas are blue, this likely implies that the soil of the Mystic Grove and Tropics is acidic.
In very old versions of BOP, Blue Hydrangeas were originally just called Hydrangea.

Scythes[edit]
  
3 ores (Replace diamonds with whatever ore), 2 sticks (Or iron ingots for Amethyst scythe)
Crafting Recipe: Put one ore on the middle left, put two ore on the top right and the top middle, put two sticks below the ore at the top right.
This tool cuts wide area with grass or leaves blocks. It is useful for clearing tree crowns, rapid farm harvesting, fast search for seeds from grass and more. Scythes will convert tall grass to medium grass to short grass to no plant successively and each change has a chance to yield seeds.

Ancient Staff Topper[edit]
  
1 Nether Star, 1 Ruby, 1 Topaz, 4 End Stone
The topper is a necessary ingredient of the Ancient Staff.

Ancient Staff Pole[edit]
  
1 Peridot, 1 Apatite (Malachite v1.2.0+), 7 End Stone
The pole is a necessary ingredient of the Ancient Staff. (This receipt does not work 1.11.2!)


Ancient Staff Handle[edit]
  
1 Sapphire, 1 Tanzanite, 5 End Stone
The handle is a necessary ingredient of the Ancient Staff.

Altar Frame[edit]

5 Large Bone Segments, 4 Obsidian
The altar frame is a building block for a structure which is used to summon the Ender Dragon.

Celestial Lens[edit]
  
5 Celestial Crystals, 4 Celestial Crystal Shards and two mud bulls

Ghastly Soul[edit]
  
4 Soulsand, 2 Blaze Powder, 2 Ghast Tears, 1 Wither Skull
This is a required ingredient for crafting a Ghastly Soul.


Soul Manipulator[edit]
  
1 Glass, 1 Ghast Tear, 1 Blaze Rod
This item can be used to capture a villager's soul in order to summon the ender dragon. Once the villager soul is captured, it is then used on a charged celestial lens at the center of an altar. The villager is sacrificed and the dragon is summoned.

Ghastly Soul Manipulator[edit]
File:RXXh2qd.png
2 Soulsand, 2 Ghastly Souls, 2 Ghast Tears, 2 Blaze Powder, 1 Soul Manipulator
This item is used in conjunction with the Altar Frame and the various collectable gems in order to summon the ender dragon. This should not be attempted in the overworld, as the ender dragon destroys all blocks save endstone and obsidian upon contact.
The ghastly soul manipulator is used on the fully constructed altar in order to charge it. After it is charged, a villager must be lured (villager soul manipulator may also be used) onto the altar in order to trap it inside for sacrifice. A second ghastly soul manipulator is used to initiate the summon once the villager soul is trapped.

Sacrificial Focus[edit]
  
One Ghastly Soul, 4 Blaze Powders, 4 Celestial Lenses
Place this block in the center of the Altar, it serves as the focus for summoning the ender dragon. It is first charged with a ghastly soul manipulator, then activated by luring a villager on it or using a villager soul manipulator on it.

Enderporter[edit]
  
4 Eyes of Ender, 4 Obsidian, 1 Amethyst Block
The Enderporter teleports you to the original spawn point and gives you buffs.


Fruit Salad[edit]
  
1 Pear, 1 Peach, 1 Berry, 1 Bowl

Shroom Salad[edit]
  
1 Toadstool, 1 Blue Milk Cap, 1 Portobello, 1 Bowl


Dart Blower[edit]
  
6 River Cane.
Crafting Recipe: Three cane on the left, three cane on the right.
The Dart Blower is a ranged weapon which uses darts for firing. It has shorter range than a bow, but fires darts much more rapidly than bow fires arrows.

Dart[edit]
  
1 thorn, 1 River Cane, 1 Feather
Crafting Recipe: Thorn on top, cane in the middle, feather on the bottom.
Darts are the projectile used with Dart Blower.


Poison Dart[edit]
  
1 Poison, 1 Dart.

Exotic Flower Band[edit]
  
2 Clover, 2 Orange Cosmos, 2 Violets, 2 Pink Daffodils.We have planned on making it so you can use any flower, but clover doesn't change. This applies for all Flower Bands, except the Dull Flower Band.

3 Barley
Crafting 3 barley will yield a standard vanilla wheat.

Fungal Jungle is a tropical biome that features mainly huge toadstools, jungle bushes, and oak trees. When in the biome, the air turns a fungal green color, likely caused by the spores of the fungi. Lots of toadstools also spawn on the ground, as well as occasional patches of dripstone and mycelium. On the mycelium patches, red mushrooms can generate. Survival is easy here, there is plenty of wood, and passive mobs do spawn here, which provides food.
Older versions of this biome instead featured huge glowshrooms, and a blue grass color. There is also a removed variant biome, the Overgrown Fungal Jungle, which contained more glowshrooms.

History[edit]


1.15.2

The Fungal Jungle was added, becoming the successor of the Nether Fungi Forest.


1.17.1

The Fungal Jungle was revamped with the addition of huge toadstools and Template:MC. The glowshroom and its variant blocks were moved to the new Glowing Grotto biome.

Fungi forest is a nether biome. It consists of huge mushrooms and other small mushrooms.

Environment[edit]
This biome is a nether version of the overworld Mushroom Island biome, featuring very tall giant red and brown mushroom, many glowshrooms, flat mushrooms, toadstools, and tiny red and brown mushrooms. Mycelial Netherrack generate along with soul sand in this biome and it's the only biome to generate the Mycelial Netherrack naturally.

History[edit]
It was added in 1.11.2, replacing the original Fungi Forest in the overworld. However, it was removed in 1.15.2, being replaced by Fungal Jungle, which also generates in the overworld.

The Fungi Forest is a forest biome made of dirt, grass, stone, and mycellium blocks. It was redesigned various times before being removed in the conversion to Minecraft 1.8. In 1.11.2, the Nether variant of the biome replaced this biome.

Description[edit]
The Fungi Forest biome is very wet and damp with some dirt blocks spawning with a thin film of water on top, when broken they revert to dirt even with silk touch. The water is a very dark green, the same color as the grass, and the sky is a teal color.  Tall oddly shaped oak trees and giant red and brown mushrooms also occur here much like they do on a Mushroom Isle. Plant life consists of all the mushrooms found in other biomes as well as short, medium, and tall grass. One can also find Mooshrooms in this biome.
Survival in the biome is easy with the readily available source of wood, beef, and mushrooms. However, mobs are able to find many hiding spots under the trees and mushrooms come day time so one should be on their guard or build fences around a cleared out area.

Gemstones are biome-specific gems introduced with Biomes O' Plenty, with the exception of Emerald which is native to Minecraft. They appear as ores, items, and decorative blocks.

Generation[edit]
Gemstone Ores can be discovered below y = 32 in their associated biomes:

Amber is found in Forest Biomes.
Emerald is found in Mountain Biomes.
Malachite is found in Swamp Biomes or in Colder Biomes like Gray Mountains.
Peridot is found in Plains Biomes.
Ruby is found in Arid Biomes. (Desert-like biomes)
Sapphire is found in Ocean Biomes.
Tanzanite is found in Cold Biomes.
Topaz is found in Lush Biomes. (Jungle-like biomes)

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Gemstone ores. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the blocks of ore rather than the Gemstones themselves. The ores drop one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe, and with fortune, the ores can drop up to four gems; with one extra per level of fortune. Amber Ore and Topaz Ore cannot be smelted.

Usage[edit]
Gemstones can be crafted into a Terrestrial Artifact. They can also be crafted into their corresponding Gemstone Blocks.

Giant flowers are larger versions of the rose and yellow flower found in Vanilla minecraft. They can only be found in the Garden biome, where they spawn instead of trees.
They each have five Giant Flower Stem blocks, which can be mined by hand. The red has 37 Giant Red Flower blocks and the yellow has 26 Giant Yellow Flower blocks, both must be mined with silk touch. 
These blocks cannot be used to made lumber or dye, and are purely decorative. (and awesome)

The Glowing Grotto is a somewhat uncommon cave biome that features both regular and huge glowshrooms, the floor is covered in mud and glowing moss blocks and carpets, and glowworm silk can be found hanging from the ceiling. All mobs that would usually generate throughout the caves can spawn here, including bats, skeletons, zombies and spiders. This biome, along with the Spider Nest, were added in 1.17, however did not generate naturally until 1.18. They could be generated with custom world type, though. It is the successor to older versions of the fungal jungle that included glowshrooms in their generation.

Glowshrooms are blue, light-emitting mushrooms found in the Glowing Grotto biome underground. Before 1.17, they were green, light-emitting mushrooms found in the Nether.

Contents

1 Usage
2 Obtaining
3 Gallery
4 History



Usage[edit]
Glowshrooms are a primarily decorative block. They emit a light level of 6,[verification needed] and always appear fully illuminated regardless of their surroundings.
Glowshrooms must be placed directly on a block, and can be placed on any full block at any light level. If the block directly below it is broken, a Glowshroom will break and drop itself. Glowshrooms cannot be planted on transparent or non-full blocks of any kind, including the full faces of blocks that otherwise aren't entirely full, such as the top of slabs.
They can also be turned into Huge Glowshrooms via the use of bone meal, in a similar manner to Vanilla's red and brown mushrooms and their huge variants, making them renewable.
Glowshrooms can be composted, with a 65% chance to raise the composter level by 1. This is 20% less than their block counterpart.

Obtaining[edit]
Glowshrooms can be obtained by breaking the naturally-generated ones in Glowing Grottos, by breaking a Glowshroom Block with anything other than a Silk Touch-enchanted tool, or by bone meal-ing a block of Glowing Moss with sufficient space around it.

Gallery[edit]

		
			
			An in-game screenshot of the Glowshroom, placed as a block. Notice how despite it's dark surroundings, the Glowshroom itself appears to be fully illuminated.
		

History[edit]


???

 Glowshrooms were added to the mod, generating in the Nether and Mushroom Fields, called Mushroom Island back then.


1.10.2

Glowshrooms now generate underground in caves.


1.15.2

 Glowshrooms were given a new texture and now generate in the Fungal Jungle. The Huge Glowshroom was also introduced.


1.17.1

Glowshrooms have been removed from the Fungal Jungle and now generate exclusively in the Glowing Grotto.

Not to be confused with their regular variant, the Glowshroom.
Glowshroom Blocks are a luminous block generated as a part of Huge Glowshrooms. They feature two unique textures, and like small Glowshrooms, always appear illuminated, regardless of their setting. They can only be obtained via a tool enchanted with Silk Touch, and if broken with anything else, will drop regular Glowshrooms. When coming into direct contact with other Glowshroom Blocks, the texture for the face that contact was made on will be replaced by a special "inside" texture.

Obtaining[edit]
Glowshroom Blocks are only obtainable via Huge Glowshrooms. These can be found in the Glowing Grotto biome, or they can be created by bone meal-ing a regular Glowshroom.
A Glowshroom Block will only drop itself if mined with a tool that has the Silk Touch enchantment. Under any other circumstance, they have a slight chance to drop a few smaller Glowshrooms, and nothing else.

Usage[edit]
Again similar to their smaller counterparts, Glowshroom Blocks are a primarily decorative block, with some luminous properties. The block appears fully illuminated regardless of context, and themselves emit a light level of 9.
Glowshroom Blocks also boast a notable niche in composting, with a whopping 85% chance to raise the current compost layer by 1. This is offset by the fact that bone meal is required itself to obtain Glowshroom Blocks consistently. However, when accounting for the vanilla Mushroom Stems that Huge Glowshrooms also generate, as well as the relatively low amount of bone meal that is required to grow a Huge Glowshroom, there is still a non-negligible chance of the player getting more bone meal than they used to create a Huge Glowshroom, if they compost every block that the aforementioned Huge Glowshroom produces.

Contents

2 Obtaining

Usage[edit]
Glowworm Silk is used as a smithing material, as mentioned above. It is one of two smithing materials added by Biomes O' Plenty, the other being Rose Quartz Chunks. Outside of this, Glowworm Silk can be placed on the underside of blocks to place it's block variant.

Smithing ingredient[edit]

Smithing recipe

All armor types can be used in this recipe;a netherite chestplate is shown as an example.Current mod loader bug makes vanilla armorusing modded trim materials lookidentical to regular armor.


Trim color palette
The following color palette is shown on the designs on trimmed armor:


Obtaining[edit]
Main Article: Glowworm Silk (Block)
Glowworm Silk is obtainable by mining it's block variant with Shears. The block variant can be obtained by exploring Glowing Grottos, placing down an existing Glowworm Silk item on the underside of any block, or by bone meal-ing the underside of a Glowing Moss Block. See the above linked article for more information.

Bugs[edit]
Armour pieces that have the Glowworm Silk material used on their armour trim will appear to have no armour trim at all in the inventory. The tooltip will still be present, but the inventory sprite will be identical to that of a similar armour piece without an armour trim.

Grasslands are flat and grassy biomes similar to plains, but with a more bluish-green grass hue. Clovers also spawn frequently here, and no trees spawn. Pigs, chickens, sheep and cows can spawn in the biome as well. There is a variant biome called Clover Patch, which also features huge clovers, azure bluets and more small clovers.

Description[edit]
The biome is a gravel beach biome with all block gravel, with the occasional shipwreck appearing.                                         You can also find pools of water in this biome.

Vegetation[edit]
There is little to no vegetation, you cannot find any trees or grass blocks in this biome.

Mobs & NPC[edit]
Mobs do not naturally spawn in this biome, and villages are absent.

Survival[edit]
This Biome is quite hard to survive in, the only sources of food are shipwrecks and fish from the ocean.

The Heathland is a relatively flat biome, home to herds of wild horses and notable for its striking amount of detail and bright Wildflowers. Some patches of the biome are covered with Pine Trees whilst the rest is covered with one-block Maple and Oak leaves. Oak trees and larger oak bushes can appear. The sky shares the same color as in Vanilla, but the grass is saturated a slight brown colour (Oak leaves appear lighter and drier). Villages can also spawn in the heathland.

This biome was removed in Build 1.11.2-6.1.0.2248 and later

content:
Hellbark Trees are found in the Undergrowth biome. These trees grow exclusively in the Nether. Saplings can be grown in all dimensions. They must be placed on a block of dirt, grass, or netherrack to grow. Most of the time they do not have a ton of leaves. All Hellbark leaves, logs, planks, etc. are fireproof 
The logs have a charred appearance and closely resemble birch logs. The leaves and planks are all black. The Hellbark hanging sign's chains are different from all the other signs, instead of being a dark gray color it appears brown. The door has a piglin head on the bottom, with its nose ring being the pull ring.

High Grass is a plant found in the Overgrown Greens biome. It resembles vanilla Tall Grass; however, High Grass impedes player movement similar to cobwebs. Though it is not as strong as cobwebs, it will prevent the player from sprinting and will drastically slow their movement.
High Grass can be any height, like sugar cane, but commonly generates between one and five blocks tall. Single-block-high plants can be distinguished from normal grass by their yellowish tips. Despite the ability of this block to slow the player, it can be destroyed instantly with no tool like any other plant block.

The Highland is a high-altitude grassland with rolling hills and very steep slopes at the edges. Vegetation includes grass and tall grass, and several animals, including cows and sheep, can spawn here. It is not a very good biome for survival, due to its lack of trees. There are a total of 2 variants in the biome family. 

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Highland Moor
1.2 Crag


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Highland Moor[edit]
Highland Moors are biomes similar to Highlands, but covered in violets and alliums. Occasional patches of oak leaves also generate. There is no other noticeable differences to the regular Highland.

Crag[edit]
The Crag is a biome with a combination of cobblestone, mossy cobblestone, stone, andesite and grass blocks as the surface. Grass covers almost every grass block that spawns, but no flowers spawn here. Goats will spawn in this biome. In older versions of BOP, the Crag was its own biome, consisting of massive and chaotic peaks that would reach almost to the build limit, with Overgrown Stone at the top.

Trivia[edit]
The old ID before 1.8 for this biome was 66.
They resemble the Scottish Highlands, which is also a council area.

The Highland Moor is a plateau-like swampy sub-biome of the Highland which has dark greenish grass.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Mobs & NPCs
1.2 Survival
1.3 Trivia


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
No animals or trees spawn in this biome. This biome is filled with lakes. Alliums, Violets, random patches of oak leaves and tall grasses are the only abundant plants here.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs do not spawn here.

Survival[edit]
Survival is hard here as there are no animals or villages and trees rarely spawn in this biome.

Trivia[edit]
Moors or moorlands are, in real life, low-vegetation grounds with acidic soil, which explains the lack of large vegetation.
Some moors are found in the UK and other numerous ones in Europe and South America.
If you have Industrialcraft (2) installed then Rubber Trees will spawn in the moor as well as the normal small trees
Before 1.8, its ID was 75
In 1.13.2, Moor was renamed into Highland Moor and made a sub-biome of the Highland.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
  The outside of a hive (1.11.2)
Hives are structures found in the Nether (from versions 1.11.x). The outside of the hive is made of Hive Block. Inside the hive are Honeycomb Block, Empty Honeycomb Block, Filled Honeycomb Block, Honey Block and Liquid Honey. Breaking an Empty Honeycomb Block gives you Empty Honeycomb. Breaking a Filled Honeycomb Block gives you Filled Honeycomb, which can be eaten. Nether Wasp can be found in and around the hive.
Right clicking on Liquid Honey with an Empty Jar creates a Honey Jar.

Types[edit]
  The inside of a hive without Liquid Honey.
There are two types of Hives, one type with a hollow inside, often with spawners within the thick walls and the other type, which is hollow on the top, but there is a level halfway through made of Honey Blocks, and below that is a pool of Liquid Honey. Each Hive generated has a 2 in 3 chance of spawning the type with Liquid Honey and Honey Blocks inside.

Trivia[edit]
  The outside of a hive (1.7.10)
It appears to be a bee hive, but wasps spawn here. They spawn from Wasp Spawners that can be found within the Hive walls and floor. 
For a short time in a very early release of BOP, hives only spawned in a certain biome, named Hellish Hive, that was removed only 5 builds later.

This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
The honeycomb block can be found in Hives generated in the Nether, and can also be crafted with 4 empty honeycombs. When broken it drops 1-3 empty honeycombs. Axes break this block the quickest.

It can be used as a furnace fuel and smelts 1 1/2 items. It can also be placed as decoration.

All blocks found in hives aside from the honey block can be used as a furnace fuel.

Hot Spring Water was a Template:MC added by the Biomes O' Plenty mod. It was usually found in the Hot Springs, Sacred Springs, Alps, Mystic Grove, Tropics, Oasis, and Wondrous Woods biomes.
It had a bright aquamarine color and gave the player a Template:MC effect. The fluid was removed in 1.13.2 and hasn't made a comeback.

Obtaining[edit]
Spring Water could only be picked up by a player using an Amethyst Bucket. It could also be obtained using pumps from other mods.
It is not possible to multiply Hot Spring Water sources like you can with Template:MC.

Notes[edit]
The Hot Springs were removed in 1.7 and re-added in 1.20.2, however with minor changes.
The Alps were removed in 1.18.
The Amethyst Bucket item was removed in 1.18.
The Wondrous Woods were removed in 1.7.
The Sacred Springs were removed in 1.13.2.

The Hot Springs biome consists of Pine trees. Thermal Calcite borders the water.  

Tips[edit]
A good seed for a Hot Spring biome is: 6104747075808482399. The coordinates for this seed are x: -126 and z: 309. This seed does not work in version 1.7.2 or above.
If you are also using a mod such as IndustrialCraft, Hot Springs biomes can be extremely useful as the lava underground is easy to pump up for energy.

History[edit]
Hot Springs was first introduced in 1.6.4 and was almost completely different. The ground was almost entirely composed of stone, with small patches of grass. It had Hot Spring Water pools that were very common. The biome was removed in 1.7.2, but re-added in 1.20.2, significally revamped.

The Huge Clover Petal is a block that appears as one of four petals arranged to cover a 2 x 2 area yielding a large four-leaf clover.  This is similar to the new Clover plant.  This plant naturally generates in the Clover Patch biome.  The Huge Clover Petal naturally generates as its full set of 4 petals. Breaking a Huge Clover Petal drops nothing while using shears on a Huge Clover Petal causes it to drop itself (a single petal).  Replanting always yields the leaf pointing southwest.  This plant does not appear to be renewable but can be generated from the new non-renewable but plentiful Clover.
The Huge Clover Petal does not allow motion and it can be stood upon just like any other block.  While not allowing motion the petal occupies only the top layer of pixels in the block and as such provides a kind of window.

Huge Glowshrooms are a type of Template:MC.
The huge glowshroom has three variants, each having a different sized cap, as well as different length stems. They feature vanilla Mushroom Stems, as well as Glowshroom Blocks.

Obtaining[edit]
Huge glowshrooms can be created by the player by using Template:MC on a glowshroom.

Natural Generation[edit]
Huge glowshrooms generate naturally in the Glowing Grotto as of Minecraft 1.17, in earlier versions they can be found in the Fungal Jungle.

History[edit]


1.15.2

Following the texture change of glowshrooms from Green to Blue, and with the new Fungal Jungle biome, huge glowshrooms were added and naturally generate within the Fungal Jungle.


1.17.1

The Fungal Jungle biome was revamped and Huge Glowshrooms were moved to the newly added Glowing Grotto.

Description[edit]
The Icy Hills biome is a frigid biome where the "trees" are made of ice. The sky in the Icy Hills biome is very foggy and the sun becomes nothing but a bright patch in the sky, as seen below.
The terrain is, as the name implies, hilly with several blocks of snow forming much of the surface above the stone below; snow blocks even make up the floor of the biome's frozen rivers.

Vegetation[edit]
There is no real vegetation in this biome.

Mobs and NPCs[edit]
Snow golems spawn naturally. Passive mobs do not spawn, hostile mobs do spawn at night and have ample "shade" to hide in during the day due to the large bases of the ice trees.

Early Survival[edit]
Survival in the Icy Hills biome is difficult as there is very little dirt, wood, or grass. Also, as passive mobs do not spawn here, the only chance is to kill zombies and eat rotten flesh, that will cause hunger. To survive successfully, it is recommended to farm animals brought from other biomes.

These are the instructions on how to install Biomes O' Plenty on both versions.

Contents

1 Java Edition

1.1 Client

1.1.1 Using MultiMC


1.2 Server (Linux)


2 Bedrock Edition



Java Edition[edit]
Client[edit]
To install Biomes O' Plenty on your client, follow these instructions (skip to step 4 if you already have your selected mod loader installed).

Download the recommended version of Forge, NeoForge or Fabric that corresponds to the Minecraft version you are using.
Open your selected mod loader's installer you just downloaded and follow the instructions to install it.
Run your selected mod loader's client once, so it generates some files and folders. This will also confirm that your selected mod loader installation worked.
Download Biomes O' Plenty from CurseForge or Modrinth, and save it to the %appdata%\.minecraft\mods folder. (make sure it is the right Minecraft version, or it will not work!)
Run your selected mod loader's client. If all goes well, you should end up at the Minecraft main menu with no errors or crashes.
If you wish to customize your BOP experience, you can alter the configuration, which generates in %appdata%\.minecraft\config\biomesoplenty after you run BOP the first time. Everything you need to know about modifying the configuration is documented on this page.
NOTE: If you are using BOP 1.18+, you need to also install TerraBlender here or here.
NOTE 2: If you are using BOP 1.20+, you need to also install GlitchCore alongside TerraBlender here or here.

Using MultiMC[edit]
If you are using MultiMC, this is how to install the mod.

First, open MultiMC, and either make a new instance or open an existing one.
Download Biomes O' Plenty on CurseForge or Modrinth.
Install your selected mod loader if you do not have it already.
Click edit instance and go to loader mods, then click add.
Select the Biomes O' Plenty file. Alternatively, simply drag the mod file in the instance window.
NOTE: If you are using BOP 1.18+, you need to also install TerraBlender here or here.
NOTE 2: If you are using BOP 1.20+, you need to also install GlitchCore alongside TerraBlender here or here.

Server (Linux)[edit]
NOTE: Currently outdated, and will not work on the latest version!
To install Biomes O' Plenty on your Linux server (e.g. Debian or Ubuntu), follow these instructions. Make sure that your Minecraft server is shut down while you follow these instructions. If you haven't installed Minecraft at all on your server yet, Scarlz's tutorial is to be recommended. Please note: the following steps have been written for and tested with Minecraft 1.11. Future versions may require adjustments.

Download the recommended installer version of Forge that corresponds to the Minecraft version you are using (yes, that's for Windows).
On a Windows machine, execute the Forge installer you just downloaded, select "Install server" and choose a temporary target directory, e.g. a new directory on your desktop.
Download the version of Biomes O' Plenty which corresponds to your versions of Minecraft and Forge, and save the jar file into the mods directory inside your directory.
Upload the entire content of your temporary directory to the server, right into the Minecraft directory. The original Minecraft jar file may be replaced, you might want to create a backup of it first.
On your server, open the file server.properties with a text editor of your choice (e.g. vim), and edit the line level-type=DEFAULT to say level-type=BIOMESOP instead; save and close the file.
Finally, run the server as usual, with the only difference that now you'll run the forge jar file instead of the original Minecraft jar file, e.g. with: java -Xmx1024M -Xms1024M -jar forge-x.xx.x-xx.xx.x.xxxx-universal.jar nogui
If you wish to customize your BOP experience, you can alter the configuration, which is located in your Minecraft directory on your server at /config/biomesoplenty after you run the server the first time. Everything you need to know about modifying the configuration is documented on this page.
NOTE: If you are using BOP 1.18+, you need to also install TerraBlender here or here.
NOTE 2: If you are using BOP 1.20+, you need to also install GlitchCore alongside TerraBlender here or here.


Bedrock Edition[edit]
NOTE: The addon is paid only in this version and costs 1340 Minecoins. If you have already bought the addon, you can skip the first part of step 2

Open up the Marketplace in-game, and search for Biomes O' Plenty. Alternatively, you can also get the addon here.
Buy the addon, then download it.
Click/tap on the "Activate Add-On!" button, which will bring the option to use the addon on a new or a existing world. Alternatively, you can manually enable the addon when creating a world, which is by going to the resource or behavior pack tabs, then clicking/tapping on the activate button, which will enable both the resource and the behavior pack, regardless which one you activated first.
Create the world. If done properly, you should see Biomes O' Plenty biomes generating in your world.
If there is an update available, the addon will update automatically, or by checking the Marketplace on occasion, in case it did not update automatically.

The Jacaranda Glade is an expansive forest biome consisting of Jacaranda Trees, some of which have fallen over and grown sprouts on top, but also the biome has giant and tiny Flowering Oaks. It also contains miniature, small, Snowblossom Trees and Cherry trees. This biome contains two flowers, blue orchids and lily of the valley. Sugarcane is also common. This biome is usually coastal.

Spawning[edit]
Cows, sheep, chickens, pigs and all the regular mobs can spawn here.

History[edit]
The biome was added in 1.16.4 and named Lavender Forest. It was similar to the lavender field but had far more jacaranda trees, regular flowering oak trees, and large versions of jacaranda trees. Overtime it was changed to look more like the jacaranda glade.
In 1.20.2 it was named to the Jacaranda Glade.

Jade Cliffs are a mountainous biome that are very densely covered with pine trees and spruce shrubs. The sky has a greenish-gray color instead of the regular color. Survival can vary from easy to hard, depending on your location. Be aware that monsters spawn more frequently in this biome's abundant dark spaces, such as beneath the overhangs of the cliffs. The abundance of wood above ground and coal below provide easy access to fuel, and grass can be harvested for wheat seeds. Cows will also spawn in this biome, providing an additional food source.
A sub-biome, Jade Grassland existed, but was removed in 1.18 due to the terrain generation overhaul.

History[edit]
The biome was removed in version 1.8.9. It would later get re-added back into the mod in 1.16.3 and use spruce trees and bushes instead of pine trees. They do however, retain the sky it had in older versions and a fog color was added. Jade Cliffs uses pine trees instead of spruce trees once again since 1.20.3. This means that this is the biome that spent the longest time not present in the mod, but then re-added.

   Jungle Spiders are hostile mobs that spawn in the tropical or jungle themed biomes like the Tropical Rainforest, Sacred Springs or Bamboo Forest biomes. They are similar to Vanilla spider mobs, only more green and much smaller.
Behavior[edit]
Unlike Vanilla spider mobs, which is neutral during daytime, jungle spiders will attack the player regardless of time or light level.  When they hit the player, the player will suffer the blindness effect for 15 seconds. This, combined with their incredible speed and small size, makes them very dangerous.

Versions[edit]
Jungle Spiders have not been present in any versions of the mod since 1.8.9.

The Kelp Forest biome is an aquatic biome filled with numerous Kelp stalks stretching from the ocean floor. The average sea-floor depth is 40, usual for an ocean floor in Minecraft. This was a very common ocean biome found near coral reefs and the Oceanic Abyss. It had gravel on its sea floor as well as more uncommonly, sand.

History[edit]
It is removed in 1.13.2 and 1.14.4, because vanilla Minecraft added kelp and dried kelp.

Tips[edit]
The best way to get around this biome is a boat, especially noting the fact that the boat cannot be hit or crashed into other blocks.

Koru is a plant found in muddy, swamp-like biomes. It is noticeable by its curly shape. When broken, there is a chance of Turnip Seeds dropping. It resembles a large fiddlehead.

Changelog[edit]
Added in version 1.2.0
Trivia[edit]
In real life, koru are the unfurling fronds of the silver fern, a plant that only grows in New Zealand. It is a symbol of new life, growth, peace, and strength.

The land of lakes is a watery forest biome, or often simply a forest.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
This biome features islands and large lakes, although these do not always spawn as they are determined by the sub-biome land of lakes marsh. There is a lot of mud on the shores, as well as gravel. It is a representation of realism showing mixed forest in North America having larger percentage of deciduous over coniferous trees. Just like in the real world it has lots of streams and lakes and occasional patches of marshland.

Vegetation[edit]
The forest in this area is primarily oak and spruce trees. Grasses a scattered about, as well as wild rice and reeds.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs spawn in this biome. There are no villages.

Survival[edit]
Survival here can be a bit difficult here due to the large amount of water and forests. Mobs can hide under the forests and it isn't easy to get around this biome.

History[edit]
)
Trivia[edit]
The old biome ID before 1.8 was 68.
This biome represents the forests of northern Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan Sort of.

Unlike its parent biome, it contains large lakes with muddy shores. Reed and Duckweed grow at the surface of the lakes. Despite this biome being relegated as a sub-biome, it sometimes spawns by itself.

Lavender Fields are somewhat flat biomes that are utterly smothered in lavender and tall lavender, with occasional flowering oak and jacaranda trees dotting the landscape. Most passive mobs, such as sheep, cows, and pigs spawn here. Bee nests sometimes spawn on trees, and the lavender everywhere is definitely going to make the bees happy. Some grass also spawns where lavender does not. There exists a variant-biome, Jacaranda Glade. Survival is easy here, due to the wood provided and the passive mobs for food. It is a great starting biome, though it may be annoying to clear out the lavender for construction.

Lily of Valley do exist on Earth, it appears in cool temperate woodlands in northern Asia, Europe and southern mountains in America.

This plant was featured in AMC's hit series "Breaking Bad"
Its formal name is Convallaria majalis.

This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.





This page needs cleanup, restyle, or its contents are significantly outdated.You can help clean it up by updating this page and bringing it up to wiki standard.

Liquid honey is found in 2 out of 3 hives generated in the Nether. It gives slowness 3 when walked in, despite flowing quite fast. It is a unique type of liquid with a special algorithm which unlike water and lava, makes it distribute evenly and there is always the same, or almost the same amount as if it were finite. (If a hole is made at the bottom of a honey-filled hive, then honey will pour out and slowly inside the hive, the level will drop).

Uses of Honey[edit]
Despite having no recipes, honey is a very important material. If one were to get stuck in the nether possibly due to a multitude of reasons, (Nether portal destroyed by ghast, etc) one can still escape the nether. Honey is important to escape as it can be used to create obsidian, simply pour it upon lava. Mods such as Natura, Tinker's Construct, or Nether Ores, also come in handy to mine the obsidian. It is also possible to use Honey for things such as traps.

Trivia[edit]
You can drown in it.
Bugs[edit]
In some versions, you cannot collect honey from honey jars or buckets.

Liquid Null is a fluid that naturally generates in the End Corruption in pools. Its appearance resembles the classic missing texture with black and purple squares. When submerged into the liquid, the player will be blinded, and see-through black and purple squares will cover the screen.

Obtaining[edit]
Liquid Null can be found in the End Corruption. Infinite sources can be created by having at least two buckets.

Usage[edit]
Liquid Null and it's corresponding item, Liquid Null Bucket, have no practical use other than converting itself and other liquids to Null Blocks.

Contact with Liquids[edit]
If Liquid Null comes into contact with any liquid, it will immediately turn it into a Null Block. When the liquid is seven blocks away from a lava source block, the Liquid Null will push back the lava until the source disappears.

Lowered Starting Health is one of the primary features of Tough As Nails. Depending on the difficulty level, you will start with less health than normal.
Peaceful: 10
Easy: 7
Normal: 5
Hard: 3
You can increase your hearts by finding Lifeblood Crystals in Nether Fortresses. You can still only have a maximum of 10 hearts, but the lowered starting health adds an additional layer of difficulty to the game.

The Lush Desert is a fairly hilly desert-like biome, comprised of orange sand and orange sandstone. Brush-like acacia trees and bushes generate here, and dune grass and desert grass cover the landscape. Wildflowers, dead grass, sprouts, and dead bushes also less commonly spawn here. Unlike the vanilla desert, it can rain in this biome. Just like most desert biomes, it's not easy to survive, empty with not much wood to harvest but lots of open space, but no passive mobs spawn here for food, though it is possible to get crops if you find a village, as they can spawn in this biome.

The Lush Savanna, previously called Poppy Field, as its name suggests, is a field full of poppies, rose bushes and sprouts. Around the landscape, blotches of ground can instead be made of coarse dirt. Survival is not easy here, as they only way to obtain wood is to find a mineshaft, and no passive mobs spawn here, making it a bad starting biome. However, this biome often spawns near a Lush Desert, so there maybe be a way to get wood.

History[edit]
It was added in 1.15.2, possibly replacing the Flower Field in 1.12.2.

The biome was renamed to ''Lush Savanna'' in 1.16.4

The Lush Swamp is similar to vanilla swamps from Minecraft's Beta 1.9.
Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation


2 Mobs & NPCs
3 Trivia
4 Gallery



Description[edit]
This swamp is very green and verdant. The water and grass are vibrant blue and green, respectively. The landscape has slight hills, ranging up to 75 on the Y axis. Pools of Poisonous Liquid may occur. Mud and Clay are common.

Vegetation[edit]
Trees in this biome are tall variations on Oak Trees, with Vines hanging off them. Tall Grass, Ferns and Bushes spawn sparsely. Red and brown Mushrooms appear, alongside Toadstools and Blue Milk Cap. Both short and tall forms Cattail spawn, as well as Sugar Cane, Wild Rice, Berry Bushes, Reeds, Damp Grass, River Cane, Koru, and various forms of lily pad. Flower here include Dandelions, Poppies, Blue Orchids, Azure Bluets, Swampflowers, and Blue Hydrangea.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Villages do not spawn in Lush Swamps.
Slimes may spawn here.

Trivia[edit]
The old Biome ID before 1.8 was 71.

Malachite is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History



Generation[edit]
Malachite Ore can be discovered in certain swampy biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Malachite Biomes. Blocks of Malachite are easily found in Gray Mountains biome in the caves. 

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Malachite Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Malachite drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Malachite Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Malachite can be crafted into a Block of Malachite for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

The Mangrove is a sub biome consisting of water with Mangrove Roots growing everywhere in large groups out of dirty blue waters. The water rarely goes below 62, making it one of the flattest biomes in Biomes O' Plenty. It is also a beach biome for tropical biomes that are bordering Oceans.

Survival Tips[edit]
In Survival Mode the cons of living in this biome are the fact that monsters survive in the water, and it is awkward to travel through by boat. However it is easier if one travels atop the trees. Mangroves are considered good spots for fishing.

History[edit]
Before BOP for 1.8, the mangrove was drastically different: Lacking its special water color and having much more sand than mud. It was also easier to get around in the biome as there was much more land. 
In a very late version of BOP for 1.11.2 the Mangrove is made no longer an oceanic biome, causing the biome ID to change. The old biome ID was 98. 
In 1.13.2 and upwards, Mangrove Trees were replaced with Mangrove Roots.
In build 1.14.4-9.0.0.207; released Tue Aug 06 03:32:09 GMT 2019; the Changelog showed forstride "added the Mangrove as a beach biome for tropical biomes." Given that the only Mangrove in the config is biomesoplenty:bayou_mangrove under sub biomes, the Changelog doesn't report the removal of the Mangrove, and updates to the Mangrove were still being made up to build 1.15.2-10.0.0.333 (Tue Feb 18 13:29:17 GMT 2020), it is likely the above is the change made to the Mangrove becoming a sub biome. While the developers still refer to this sub biome as simply Mangrove, the parent biome; the Bayou; is indicated in its namespaced ID. Just like how the namespaced ID of Pumpkin Patch is biomesoplenty:seasonal_pumpkin_patch because it is a sub biome of the Seasonal Forest.
Minecraft Live 2021 announced a revamp to swamps coming in 1.19, adding mangrove swamps, but with different generation.

  Mangrove Tree with roots exposed
The Mangrove Tree can be found growing in clusters throughout the mangrove biome. They have bright white wood and planks. 

Raw wood: Mangrove wood
Planks: Mangrove planks
Crafting: Slabs, Stairs, Fences, Fence Gates, Doors
Mangrove saplings can only be grown on sand in older versions. When a sapling grows, it produces a "root structure" made of mangrove wood which extends several blocks into the ground and will destroy any block, including bedrock, in its path. In newer versions, you use bonemeal in the centre of a 3x3 patch of Mangrove saplings, but you may want to put the saplings one or two blocks lower if you want a shorter tree.
Do not plant mangroves near anything you do not want to lose. It won't destroy the contents of a chest, but it will break the chest and the items may despawn on the ground.

History[edit]

summary: Maple Trees can be found in the Seasonal Forest, Pumpkin Patch, Maple Woods, Tundra, and Bog biomes. They come in three variants, Red Maple, Orange Maple, and Yellow Maple. Red Maple can be found in all the biomes listed, however the Tundra and Bog biomes only spawn tiny scrubs with very few leaves....
content:
Maple Trees can be found in the Seasonal Forest, Pumpkin Patch, Maple Woods, Tundra, and Bog biomes. They come in three variants, Red Maple, Orange Maple, and Yellow Maple. Red Maple can be found in all the biomes listed, however the Tundra and Bog biomes only spawn tiny scrubs with very few leaves. Orange Maple can be found in the Seasonal Forest and Pumpkin Patch biomes, while Yellow Maple can only be found in the Seasonal Forest. Yellow Maple Leaves can be obtained from the Aspen Glade but do not have maple logs. When grown via sapling, maple trees do not produce Maple Leaf Piles. The tree's leaves produce falling leaf particles that differ in color depending on the leaf color. They're also very similar to oak tree shapes.

Resources[edit]
Logs: Maple Logs

Leaves: Red Maple Leaves, Orange Maple Leaves, Yellow Maple Leaves

Mediterranean Forests are lush biomes with Cypress trees, dark oak trees, differently shaped oak trees, shrubs (can contain flowering oak leaves), and an abundance of grass and bush plants. Peonies, dandelions and poppies also spawn frequently in this biome. Calcite replaces dirt in underwater portions of the biome. Survival is very easy here, due to the abundance of wood, and passive mobs for food. Villages can spawn here, giving easy access to food like carrots and potatoes.
This biome used to be called Grove, however it was renamed to Mediterranean Forest in 1.18 due to the addition of the vanilla Grove biome.

Not to be confused with the Mesa biome from vanilla Minecraft, or Mesa Bryce biome from vanilla Minecraft, which from 1.13 are known as "Badlands" and "Eroded Badlands" respectively.

The Mesa biome is a rather mountainous biome, which is covered in Red Rock with occasional tiny cacti and Desert Grass all over. The sky is pinkish red, and the peaks average around 120 blocks in height. Unlike vanilla mesa biomes, this biome had no clay layers.
Survival would be rather difficult in this biome, due to there being no wood or similar crafting materials, and lack of Grass to farm. It is recommended to find a different biome to get resources from, and make a base here if you want to live in this biome.

Moss
	
		
		
	
	

	Moss



Moss is a flat block found on vertical surfaces in most swamp-type and some forest-type biomes, like Bayou or Temperate Rainforest. It can be used to make Green Dye, Mossy Cobblestone and Mossy Stone Brick. If one unit of moss is placed, it will replicate itself by spreading to adjacent surfaces, similar to the mechanics in mushroom-growing. You can harvest moss by left clicking it with Shears. The Moss was removed might be due to the Moss Stone and Mossy Stone Bricks can be crafted with vines instead.

Info[edit]
Mountains range from 150 to 198 on the Y-axis. The grass color in this biome is teal and the biome is covered with ice and snow.

Vegetation[edit]
The trees consist of Spruce trees, but there are some fir trees in this biome. 

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs, including Wolves, can spawn here, but Polar Bears are the only hostile mobs that can spawn here.

Survival[edit]
Surviving in this biome is fairly easy. Wood is common here, minerals can be found here but the food is hard to obtain. Be careful of the steep drops on the edge of the biome, albeit the steep drops here are a little harder to climb than most other high biomes.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
The mud block is a part of Biomes O' Plenty to make its swamp-like biomes more realistic. It uses the slime block properties (including bounce, but not much. It has the slime block sounds as well.). 
It was removed in 1.19 due to the addition of mud to vanilla Minecraft. The mud that would normally generate in Wetlands, Bayous, and Glowing Grottos was replaced with vanilla mud.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.

The Mystery Music Disc is an unnamed music disc introduced by BOP. The disk takes the shape of a normal Minecraft disc, except it is caked in mud and almost unrecognizable. Within the mod files, the sound file named "corruption.ogg" exists, most likely being the real disc name. To craft it, you'll put the Wanderer Music Disc in the middle and 8 mud balls surrounding on it.

"Wanderer" refers to both a song composed by Tim Rurkowski, and a music disc that plays the song when inserted in a jukebox. The music disc is obtained by completing the Wanderer advancement.

Usage[edit]
Like all vanilla music discs, using the "Wanderer" music disc on a jukebox causes the jukebox to play the song.
If the player places a redstone comparator besides a jukebox playing "Wanderer", it will emit a redstone signal of 15.

Mycelial Netherrack are a new mycelium like blocks found in Fungi Forest (Nether), in the nether.

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Natural Generation
3 Characteristics
4 Gallery



Obtaining[edit]
Mycelial netherrack requires a pickaxe to be mined, in which case it will drop netherrack. When mined without a pickaxe, it will drop nothing. If mycelial netherrack is mined with a silk touch enchanted pickaxe, it will drop itself.

Natural Generation[edit]
They naturally generate as the ground block in the fungi forest biome in later versions of 1.11.2 or later.
Characteristics[edit]
This block is a nether version of Mycelium block, with mycelium grass on top covering netherrack, much like Overgrown Netherrack.
Unlike netherrack, the mycelium netherrack does not burn eternally when set on fire.
This block was made most likely to be the ground of new nether biome.

Mystic Groves are rare biomes filled with magic, oak and dark oak trees, flowers, and giant red mushrooms, with a mystic twilight pink color to the air. Alliums, lilacs, blue hydrangeas, pink daffodils and glowflowers spawn frequently here, giving the biome a colorful atmosphere. The water in this biome is also pink. Survival is easy here due to the abundance of wood and grass for wheat seeds. Witches spawn here at night, allays and a special spectral wolf variant can also be found here.

History[edit]
In very early versions of BOP, Magic Trees were more like pine trees and they had different textures. Before BOP 1.13.2, Mystic Grove biomes had Poisonous Liquid pools and Hot Spring Water pools.
In 1.6.4, there is a sub-biome called Thinned Mystic Grove. It contains fewer trees but was removed in 1.7.2.

An oasis was a sub-biome of the vanilla Desert biome with small pools of water surrounded by bright green Sandy Grass blocks and Palm Trees. It rarely spawned inside small deserts.
Before 1.8, Spring Water pools also spawned in oasis, but were much rarer than the normal water pools.
Surviving in the desert was easier with the availability of wood and the possibility of farming, but the sandy landscape may have needed some terraforming for large scale farming.

The Ominous Woods biome is a dark, heavily wooded biome with scattered pools of dark purple water. Umbran and Dead Trees grow here, along with a variety of other vegetation. This biome is rare, having a similar chance to the Mystic Grove biome. Grass is found on the ground, mixed with mushrooms and Dead Leaves. Illusioners, normally unused vanilla mobs will spawn in this biome and can cause threats because of his ability to go invisible and make clones, as well as the ability to blind a player. The bramble thorns found here can harm the player, and the Wither Roses apply the wither effect when a player walks through it. This is one of the most difficult biomes to survive in for beginners. There is very little to eat, and both the bramble thorns and wither roses will sap hunger and health if the player is careless.

History[edit]
Prior to the 1.8 version of BoP, Dark Wood was used instead of Umbran Wood, which has a slightly different texture. Cave Spiders, hostile wolves, and Endermen were the only mobs that spawn in this biome. Thick Ominous Woods was a sub-biome to this biome. It contained Thick Dark Trees which were much taller, that is more common there than in the normal Ominous Woods.
There was a sub-biome, Ominous Mire, a low-lying version with less umbran trees, however it was removed in 1.18. It also had watergrass.

The Orchard is a sparsely forested biome with distinct grass and foliage colors, and characteristic flowering oak trees. Rose bushes and oxeye daisies spawn in this biome, as well as sprouts. There is not a lot to eat here immediately, until a farm is set up. However, the large areas of grass and the ponds allow for quick farm-building, making it a relatively easy biome to survive in. The leaves can also be broken to obtain apples for consumption.

History[edit]
Before Minecraft 1.8, Apple Trees dominated the biome, in which the leaves had chances of dropping an apple, (please see Apple Tree for more details of the tree and the leaves). Before it was a sub-biome of the Plains, now it is redesigned and independent. However, they were removed because they made it too easy to gain apples. The only trees were small oak trees, and they were much more spread out. Orchards were also sub-biomes of the vanilla Plains biome, but were made separate in 1.8. In 1.10, the trees were modified to be more spread out, and small shallow lakes appear across the biome sometimes too. In 1.13.2, Orchard was once again made into a sub-biome of the Plains biome, and in 1.18, it was changed back to its own biome again.

Gallery[edit]

		
			
			
		
		
			
			Orchard with Shaders in 1.12.2 Minecraft
		

Trivia[edit]
The BoP Orchard is different from real-life orchards: ones in real-life are usually human-made for commercial purposes. There are a few instances of apple orchards growing naturally, however.
The new design of the biome is a combination of the removed Dense Forest, the old Orchard, and possibly the Overgrown Greens.

Origin Grass
	
		
		
	
	

	Origin Grass Block



Origin Grass can only be found in the Origin Hills biome, and has the appearance of the grass blocks found in Classic versions of Minecraft.
Unlike normally occurring grass blocks, Origin grass blocks do not change color in different biomes and do not respond to bonemeal.
It is also not possible to put Biomes O' Plenty flowers and grasses on origin grass, although it is possible to place all saplings and some Vanilla plants like roses and ferns. Sugar cane can be placed and grown on this block even if it is not adjacent to water, making it useful for paper farms. Also, sheep without their wool can't eat this kind of grass, making it useless for wool farms.

Origin Trees are rarer versions of oak trees found only in the Origin Valley. These trees have the older texture of their sapling and leaves but keep the same oak wood. They are the exact same as oak trees, except with the leaves changed. They have the same versions of oak tree shapes from the regular oak, fancy oak, and "balloon" oak shapes.

Origin Valleys are very rare island biomes that are reminiscent of alpha Minecraft before actual biomes were added. The original roses that were removed in Minecraft 1.7 can be found in this biome, alongside dandelions. The water, sky, grass and foliage colors are the same as in alpha, and the ground is instead made out of origin grass blocks. Origin trees spawn in this biome, but they still give regular oak wood, it's just the leaves that are different. Survival is easy here, due to the passive mobs that spawn, and availability of wood. Though, survival here on your first night will not occur often due to the rarity of this biome.
There are a total of two biomes in the family.

Variants[edit]
Wintry Origin Valley[edit]
Wintry Origin Valley is a snowy variant of the Origin Valley, resembling the removed "Winter mode" from alpha Minecraft 1.1.2. It only generates in a snowy climate, mostly near Frozen Oceans.

Notice![edit]
If you are using OptiFine, it is not recommended to enable fancy grass while in this biome, as it will give the sides of the grass an ugly grey texture, as it does not detect the origin grass texture.

The Outback is a hilly desert-like biome filled with patches of Sandy Grass and Red Sand. Desert Temples may spawn in this biome.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
The landscape is a patchwork of Red Sand and yellow-green Sandy Grass blocks, with Grass growing in abundance. Pools of water and lava spawn sporadically. The Outback Biome is supposed to resemble areas of Central Australia commonly referred to as the Outback. 

Vegetation[edit]
Grass can be found on the ground, with a scatter of tiny Acacia Trees. There are lots of Tiny Cactus which can be obscured by surrounding vegetation.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Few mobs spawn here, however villages will spawn. One of the more common mobs will be animals like Kangaroos.

Survival[edit]
Survival is a challenge, because the Acacia trees are only two blocks tall, and animals are scarce. However, there is enough wood to make a sizeable house, and wheat can be grown using grass seeds. Small Cacti provide a minor hazard while exploring. 

History[edit]
Most of the surface was covered by Hardened Sand in version 1.8, and elevation can vary by about a dozen blocks. As of 1.9, the hardened sand was removed. Grass blocks and red sand is the surface of this biome (1.9+).

The biome was removed in 1.16.4.

Overgrown Greens, formerly called Clover Patch, is a biome characterized by large four-leaf Clovers, very thick High Grass and huge flowers, which make traversing this biome on foot somewhat of a challenge. 
Other ground cover includes clover, short grass, pink daffodils and torchflowers, and the ground itself is primarily grass with large swathes of coarse dirt. Cows, sheep, and chickens spawn regularly here.

Obtaining[edit]
Althrough Overgrown Netherrack can be mined with a pickaxe, it will drop Netherrack when broken unless the pickaxe is enchanted with Silk Touch.
Natural Generation[edit]
They generate naturally exclusively in Undergarden biome.
Characteristics[edit]
This block is a nether version of normal grass block, with grass on covering netherrack.
Unlike netherrack, the overgrown netherrack does not burn eternally when set on fire.
The color of Overgrown netherrack grass does not change when placed in different biomes.
