Overgrown Stone is a new block to Biomes O' Plenty. It "replaces Smoldering Grass Blocks" according to the github update log, even though normal stone doesn't appear in the Nether. Like normal grass, the color of Overgrown Stone's grass cover will change based on its biome.


Obtaining[edit]
Although Overgrown Stone can be mined with a pickaxe, it will drop Cobblestone when broken unless the pickaxe is enchanted with Silk Touch.

Natural Generation[edit]
The overgrown stone block is the ground block of the new Crag biome.
In Alps Foothills biome, this block generates with snow on top.
Generates in patches in the Overgrown Cliffs and Chaparral biomes.
History[edit]
It was added in 1.9, and removed in 1.13.2.

summary: Palm Trees are somewhat tall tropical trees. They can be found in the Tropics and Lush Desert biomes. They can grow straight up or slightly curved. The texture of the leaves depict giant leaves with minimal visibility through them. The leaves grow out in eight total segments, four segments on the to...
content:
Palm Trees are somewhat tall tropical trees. They can be found in the Tropics and Lush Desert biomes. They can grow straight up or slightly curved. The texture of the leaves depict giant leaves with minimal visibility through them. The leaves grow out in eight total segments, four segments on the top of the tree, and four segments that droop down lower on the tree. The wood of the tree is a bright orange color. The doors and trapdoors are screen doors in a crossed X pattern.

Peridot is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History



Generation[edit]
Peridot Ore can be discovered in grassland biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Peridot Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Peridot Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Peridot drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Peridot Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Peridot can be crafted into a Block of Peridot for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

content:
Persimmon Tree






This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.

These trees produce persimmon fruit. Just like apple trees, there are three leaf stages: flowering, unripe green fruit, and ripe orange fruit. Only the final stage will yield fruit. You can pick the fruit by right-clicking it. Persimmon trees are composed of oak wood. They were removed with Apple Trees in 1.8 because of the ease of getting fruit from fruit trees.
Persimmon Trees can be found in the (now removed) Autumn Hills biome and the Dead Forest biome. Dying Trees will also drop Persimmons.
Raw wood: Oak wood
Planks: Oak Planks
Crafting: slabs, stairs

Persimmon Fruit[edit]
Persimmon fruit are a food, similar to apples, that fall from a variety of trees. They refill 5 hunger, or 2 1/2 shanks. Persimmon Trees and Yellow Autumn Birches are two of the trees that can drop Persimmons.

content:
Pine Trees used to be removed in 1.13.2 but have been added in 1.20.3. They are found in the Dryland and Jade Cliffs biomes. These trees are fairly long and have branches coming out of the trunk. The leaf block of the tree depicts little sticks connecting to the leaves. The logs can have holes in the bark which surround all sides of it. The wood itself is a swamp-green color, and the doors and trapdoors are paper screen doors.

Leaves: Pine Leaves





Trivia[edit]
Pine Trees used to be found in the now removed Shield and Mountain biomes.
Before, these trees couldn't be grown in Lush Deserts, or any wetland biome.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.

Pinecones are items that drop from Fir Leaves.

History[edit]
It was added probably in 1.6.4, as a block and as an item. Block form used to spawn under Fir Trees, and it would drop an item form if destroyed. In 1.8, block form was removed in favor of having a chance of dropping from leaves, just like Apples from Oak Trees in vanilla Minecraft. It was removed entirely in very later builds in 1.12.2.

content:
Two Pixies flying around in the Mystic Grove biome.
Pixies are flying mobs exclusive to the Mystic Grove biome. They are passive, and will fly around and shine brightly. They drop Pixie Dust upon death. Pixie Dust can be used to make a potion called Ambrosia. Pixies can be captured in an Empty Jar, and then it will become a Pixie Jar. Pixies spawn at night. They also have their own exclusive particle effect, which promptly helps the small critters be seen better.
This mob has since been moved from Biomes O' Plenty to the mod Familiar Fauna,a mod created by the same development team.
They once were scattered all over the Promised Land before it was removed.

Poisonous liquid is a purplish liquid found in small lakes in several biomes. Hunger and poison debuffs affect the player when in contact with poisonous liquid. It can be contained in a bucket.

Contents

1 Locations

1.1 Lush Swamps
1.2 Bogs
1.3 Ominous Woods
1.4 Mystic Groves


2 Properties



Locations[edit]
Poison is found naturally in various swamp biomes. It can be found commonly in Lush Swamps, Bogs, Ominous Forests, and Mystic Groves.

Lush Swamps[edit]
Poison is commonly found in Lush Swamps as small pools usually 1-2 blocks deep. They can grow sugar cane, river cane (removed), reed, and cattail. They can harbor lily pads.

Bogs[edit]
In Bogs, poison liquid ponds are very common. They are often surrounded with mud.

Ominous Woods[edit]
In Ominous Woods, occasional poison pools may appear. 

  Poison pools in Ominous Woods.
Mystic Groves[edit]
In Mystic Groves, water appears purple, but it is not poison. However, poison pools still generate in Mystic Groves. Water is a more animated and bright purple, while poison will appear murky with faded color.

  Water in a Mystic Grove.
  Poison in a Mystic Grove.
  Purple water in a Mystic Grove.
Properties[edit]
  Liquid flow comparison. Poison, at the bottom, flows 4 blocks.
Poison only flows 4 blocks from its source block. In survival, movement is impeded in poison due to damage taken. However, in creative mode, poison impedes movement as much as water. It is not renewable.
You take half a heart of damage per second when swimming in poison. Due to rapidly getting hurt, you cannot swim as quickly. You get hunger and poison for 5 seconds upon touching poison.
When water or any other liquid flows across poison, the poison disappears and becomes mud. The same is true if poison flows on water. The mud can be broken and drops balls of mud, which can be thrown.

The Polar Chasm is a nether biome covered in Hardened Ice and Snow. The sky has a blue tint compared to the other Nether biomes. There is no vegetation and glowstone deposits are replaced with regular ice. Ice and hot spring water pools can also spawn here.
It used to be the rarest Nether biome in the mod, being so hard to find that the creator Forstride implied that they made it so rare so nobody would find it. It was also the only "cold" biome introduced in the Nether by BOP.

Contents

1 History
2 Gallery

2.1 Newer (1.11.2)
2.2 Older (1.7.10 and below)





History[edit]
In 1.7.10 and earlier, mushrooms spawned in Polar Chasm biomes and only snow covered the biome. Since it was so rare, many people thought it was removed in 1.7.10 and that it would not return in 1.11.2. The old biome ID was 58.
The biome was readded in 1.11.2, but appears to be significantly more common.
This biome was removed once again in Biomes O' Plenty version 1.12.2-7.0.1.2357.

The Prairie biome is largely flat, with grassy plains, goldenrods, and large brush oaks interwoven with tall grass. Some small shrubs spawn here as well. Most Vanilla passive mobs spawn naturally in this biome. Villages can spawn in this biome as well. This biome is fairly easy for survival, due to the presence of wood and animals for food. Grass can also be broken for wheat seeds, and water pools do spawn here which will allow for farming.
There are a total of two biomes in the biome family.

Contents

Variants[edit]
Pasture[edit]
The Pasture biome is a biome similar to the prairie, but with no trees or goldenrods, and the landscape is almost completely covered in barley. In 1.17, it was renamed to Golden Prairie, but then renamed back to Pasture in 1.18.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.Notes: Removed in Minecraft 1.7.2

The Promised Land was a dimension reachable by using the Ancient Staff in the Overworld. Like the other special dimensions, the Nether and the End, the Promised Land is made almost entirely of unique blocks and has properties not found in the Overworld.

Description[edit]
The Promised Land is made of floating islands which spawn infinitely and horizontally in a sunset-colored sky. Large islands will spawn every several hundred blocks, with patches of clouds (made from Cloud Blocks) between each large island. Unlike the Nether, clocks work fine, but have no use as it is permanently noon. Beds cannot be used or it will cause an explosion, just like in the Nether.
The floating islands are made of Skystone covered in Purified Dirt and Purified Grass. Pools of water and Spring Water, caverns, cliffs, holes and small islands break up the scenery. Travel is difficult, and if you fall you will spawn high in the Overworld, usually resulting in death by fall damage unless you are lucky enough to land in water.
Amethyst Ore is scattered throughout the Skystone of the islands, and Celestial Crystal grows similar to Glowstone, by hanging from the underside of the islands.
There are four biomes in the Promised Land: Blessed Bog, Wondrous Woods, Majestic Meadow, and Sublime Shrubland. Vegetation on the surface is determined by biome, although Loftwood Trees, unique to the Promised Land, can be found in most places.
No mobs will spawn in the Promised Land, saved for birds flying around everywhere, and pixies floating about in the Blessed Bog and Sublime Shrubland.

Removal[edit]
As of BOP For 1.7.2, the Promised Land is no longer in game, this sparked controversy throughout r/Biomesoplenty and the modding community, however it was removed because it created too much lag. Many of the blocks in the biomes have been removed or have no use. However the developers have since returned the use for stuff such as Celestial Crystals and Amethyst in the End.

content:
This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
Puddles are created when it rains. Essentially, random blocks of dirt/grassy dirt on the surface are destroyed and replaced by water source blocks. These "puddles" remain after the rain has stopped. They will theoretically not be created if Griefing (any form of block breaking other than directly by a player) is turned off. (Verification needed.)
If puddles are enabled, you need not worry about them littering your world; after it stops raining they will eventually turn back into dirt.
This effect can be removed in misc.cfg at within the biomesoplenty config file by setting B:"Enable Puddles During Rain"=true to B:"Enable Puddles During Rain"=false. This may or may not work for versions other than 1.2.1.434 depending on if the correlating line of code is within the misc.cfg file.

Natural Generation[edit]
Pus Bubbles can only be found in the Visceral Heap.

Breaking[edit]
Pus Bubbles can only be obtained by using an item with silk touch.

Placing[edit]
Pus Bubbles can only be placed on Flesh, Porous Flesh, Netherrack, and Bone Blocks.

Usage[edit]
Other than decoration, the Pus Bubble by itself has no real uses.

The Quagmire is a marshy, muddy biome with no resources.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival


2 History
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
The ground is composed of a mix of Mud, Loamy Dirt, and some Loamy Grass. Large, marshy brown ponds are frequent, with Reeds and lily pads. Very sadly, no trees grow here.

Vegetation[edit]
Koru and water lilies spawn here, and Grass and Reeds are very common. Trees do not spawn here naturally.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive mobs do not spawn here. Bad Witch Huts may spawn.

Survival[edit]
Survival here is difficult, as there are no trees and food is NOWHERE. The mud can be crafted into mud bricks, which can be used to build shelter, but other than that there are no useful resources here.

History[edit]
It used to be possible to craft mud tools and armor from Mud Balls. These were not very practical, though, as they had very low durability and strength.
Before 1.8 trees made from Dead Wood naturally generated throughout the quagmire. It had a brown sky and a greyish-white fog. Also no animals spawned there.
In 1.7.2 and 1.7.10, Quagmire used to be sub-biome of the Sludgepit. It was removed in 1.16.1

Quicksand is a liquid block found in desert and savanna type biomes, including the vanilla Desert and the Tropical Rainforest biome. Quicksand acts much like Hot Spring Water as it cannot be made into an infinite source, but can still be collected by a bucket.
Quicksand spawn in water pool-shaped holes and are mostly 1 block deep. Like Cobwebs, if a player walks into quicksand they will be slowed dramatically and begin to sink into the block. However, unlike cobwebs, quicksand will suffocate the player if their head dips into the block. If another liquid touches Quicksand, it will turn into Mud. Going under it will show the same appearance as if you went underwater.

Contents

1 Before 1.9
2 Tips & Uses

2.1 Mob Grinders


3 Gallery

3.1 Current
3.2 Old





Before 1.9[edit]
Before 1.9 it was a solid block that was the full size of an ordinary block, it was mined with a spade as well. Before 1.8 it had a different texture, almost the same as sand but slightly more yellow.

Tips & Uses[edit]
If you do fall in, it takes a little less than 30 seconds to fall completely sink a pit of quicksand. You can't swim upwards out of quicksand, but you can remove the Quicksand with sponges, or use another liquid-filled bucket on the ledges so that the Quicksand turns into mud. You also can escape by using Ender Pearl to teleport to safe block.
Of course, the best way to get out of quicksand is to not get into it in the first place. If you are traversing a desert or the like on foot, then keep your eyes open for quicksand patches. If you find yourself frequently crossing a desert, remove all the quicksand from your path - or make a bridge.
Quicksand can be placed in a one layer deep pit as a means of trapping mobs. Mobs will walk into the pit and be unable to climb out. You can do a two-block deep trap for hostile mobs to kill them too. Hostile mobs do not burn in quicksand though.
Endermen appear unable to teleport out of quicksand (citation needed)

Mob Grinders[edit]
Quicksand may be used to make cheap, effective mob grinders. Cave spiders are able to survive passing through twelve blocks of quicksand with only a half heart at the end, making them the most effective mob to grind for experience. (They can be killed with a single punch)

Rainbow Birch Trees are rare trees exclusively found in the Auroral Garden. These trees grow in a variety of shapes and colors. They are similar to how Oak trees grow in terms of shape. Color-wise, these trees vary depending on their position in the world. Their color can also be changed when any form of snow is placed on top of the block, if a form of snow is placed on top of them the color will turn lighter, the change of color has a depth of 2 blocks before the color change stops. Rainbow Birch leaves also emit a light level of 8.

Rainforests are hot and very humid biomes with lots of ferns and mahogany trees. Occasional puddles, dripleaves, orange cosmos, and small jungle trees spawn here. Cocoa beans can spawn on the jungle trees, as well as vines. Melons can also be found on the surface frequently. Parrots spawn here, but no other passive mobs do. Jungle pyramids can spawn in this biome, similar to the vanilla jungle. The terrain can sometimes be somewhat hilly in this biome. Survival is not adequate here, due to parrots being the only mobs that spawn, and the dense canopy sometimes providing darkness for mobs to spawn.
There are a total of two biomes in the biome family.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Rocky Rainforest
1.2 History


2 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Rocky Rainforest[edit]
Rocky Rainforests, previously called Rainforest Cliffs, and before called Overgrown Cliffs, are variants of the Rainforest with less trees, lots of bushes, and parts of the ground made of terracotta. Sprouts also cover the landscape.

History[edit]
This biome, when it was added, it was called Tropical Rainforest, it had a tropical green sky and the trees used Jungle Wood, because there wasn't any Mahogany Wood back then. In 1.6.4, A red-orange fog was also added. In 1.7.10, Mahogany Wood replaced the Jungle Wood on the trees. In 1.8.9, the sky color and the fog color were removed. In 1.16.4, the Tropical Rainforest was renamed to Rainforest, removing the original Rainforest biome.

The rainforest is a temperate forest biome with distinctly darker green grass and leaves.  

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
The biome contains lots of large mountains, cliffs, valleys, and ponds of water. 

Vegetation[edit]
The biome has many lakes with wetland plants around, such as Lily Pads. Both Birch and Flowering Oak Trees spawn here, sometimes featuring Vines. Orange Cosmos, Dandelions, Blue Orchids, and Rafflesia grow on the ground.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Parrots and ocelots spawn in this biome, alongside common passive mobs such as chickens.

Survival[edit]
Getting from place to place in the biome can be difficult. Crossing bodies of water and climbing sheer cliffs is often necessary to find food and shelter. Though dense, there are small breaks in the forest that are suitable for building. Jungle Temples will spawn in this biome, providing some useful loot.

Red Rock Cobblestone is a block commonly used for decoration. It resembles a cracked, uneven surface, much like the block it is based off of.


Contents

1.1 Mining


2 Usage

2.1 As a Smelting Ingredient
2.2 As a Crafting Ingredient

Obtaining[edit]
Mining[edit]
Red Rock Cobblestone can only be obtainable by entering a Mesa biome, and using any type of pickaxe, (but not one with the Silk Touch enchantment) to mine the commonly found Red Rock.

Usage[edit]
Red Rock Cobblestone doesn't have any use besides decorating your house or constructing any type of building. The block itself only has a couple of recipes, the which are stairs and slabs. It may also be re-smelted to have Red Rock, like its vanilla counterpart.

The Redwood Forest is a densely wooded biome filled with Redwood Trees. Most of the ground is podzol, broken occasionally by patches of moss blocks. Ferns cover the surface, and occasional tall ferns. Survival is easy with the amount of wood and shelter. Passive mobs do spawn within the forest. Most of these forests have many low hills inside the biome, this makes building large flat areas hard, and may also make them hard to navigate through at times. 
It is based off of the redwood forests found in California.

History[edit]
Before 1.10.2, the single redwood trees didn't exist and before 1.8, redwood trees were much duller and had a different shape.

summary: Redwood Trees are the tallest trees in the mod, growing at around 50–60 blocks tall. These trees can be found in the Redwood Forest biome. content:
Redwood Trees are the tallest trees in the mod, growing at around 50–60 blocks tall. These trees can be found in the Redwood Forest biome. They are among the most plentiful trees in terms of wood. The saplings can be grown with either one sapling, or four arranged in a 2x2 grid. One sapling Redwood trees are much shorter and yield Redwood Logs, while the Four sapling trees have Redwood Wood.
Version 1.2.0+ - 
As of version 1.2.0, only one Redwood sapling is required to grow a tree.
Before version 1.2.0 - 
To spawn a redwood, the nine saplings must be planted in a 3x3 square. They must be planted on grass blocks, not dirt, and must have one extra block on each side.

  Illustrated by the yellow blocks. The red blocks being where the saplings are planted.

Reeds are usually found in the Fen, Bog and Quagmire biomes. They are decorative. For the plant named Reed up until version 1.1.0, see River Cane.
In order to grow reeds, one must place them in a 1-block high body of water.
[1.7] Pick up Reeds with Shears (not by Hand).  Place Reed on block above water or on surface of water block.  If you are in water one block deep then placing a Reed will place it on the block you are standing in.

  I placed them kind of by accident
[1.12.2] You might be able to place them! But it's oddly specific. There's a weird bug. I was able to place them if I was flying at 4 blocks above the water in creative mode, but I could not place them if I was on the ground/in the water. I also added a screenshot I took for proof. I promise this worked, I was very surprised when one actually placed.

Rock Formations are relatively new items, added in 1.9, these naturally generate 3-6 blocks high in some caves. They serve as replacements of Stalagmites and Stalactites which were in older versions.
They can only be placed on stone, but they can be placed on top or on the bottom of a stone block. They can join up to make merged stalactites and stalagmites.

Rose Quartz Buds are blocks found in the Crystalline Chasm. They have three different types, large, medium, and small. They do not grow into Rose Quartz Clusters or their larger variants. Each bud emits light, large ones emit a light level of 7, medium ones emit a light level of 6, and small ones emit a light level of 5.


Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Natural Generation
1.2 Breaking


2 Placing
3 Usage



Obtaining[edit]
Natural Generation[edit]
Rose Quartz Buds can only be found in the Crystalline Chasm.

Breaking[edit]
The only way to get Rose Quartz Buds is by breaking them with any item that has silk touch applied to it. Though, using a pickaxe with silk touch can break them the fastest.

Placing[edit]
Rose Quartz Buds can be placed on top of, under, and on the side of blocks.

Usage[edit]
Other than decoration, Rose Quartz Buds by themselves have no real uses.

Rose Quartz Clusters are blocks exclusively found in the Crystalline Chasm. They're a re-skinned version of the Amethyst Cluster with a scarlet color. It emits a light level of 8.


Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Natural Generation
1.2 Breaking


2 Placing
3 Usage



Obtaining[edit]
Natural Generation[edit]
Rose Quartz Clusters can only be found in the Crystalline Chasm.

Breaking[edit]
When broken via hand or pickaxe, Rose Quartz Clusters drop Rose Quartz Chunks. When breaking with anything but a pickaxe, two rose quartz chunks are dropped, but when using a pickaxe four rose quartz chunks are dropped. The amount of rose quartz chunks dropped can be affected by fortune. When using silk touch, the Rose Quartz Cluster itself is dropped.

Placing[edit]
Rose Quartz Clusters can be placed on top of, under, and on the side of blocks.

Usage[edit]
Rose Quartz Clusters can be mined to get Rose Quartz Chunks.

Ruby is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History



Generation[edit]
Ruby Ore can be discovered in desert biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Ruby Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Ruby Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Ruby drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Ruby Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Ruby can be crafted into a Block of Ruby for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.
They can be used in the Numismatic Dynamo with the augment Lapidary Calibration if you have the mod thermal expansion installed, and generates 200,000 RF per ruby.

The Sacred Springs is a lush tropical biome. It is featured with huge Sacred Oak Trees and large quantities of hot spring pools.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
Sacred Oak Trees naturally spawn here. There are dark green grass and intermittent springs spouting from hills. Lots of hot spring pools can be found in the biome. Since the huge Oak Trees block the sunlight, hostile mobs may spawn in the day.
Hot Spring Water spawns throughout the terrain, as well as Jungle Temples.

Vegetation[edit]
Both Flowering and Sacred Oak Trees make up the canopy. Various water lilies are distributed throughout the springs, and Rafflesia grows on the ground.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Regular passive mobs like pigs and sheep can spawn in the Sacred Springs biome, but mob spawning tends to be somewhat limited because of the mass amounts of leaves, which mobs can't spawn on.

Survival[edit]
It is not very hard to survive here because of the large quantities of trees and animals. Adventurers are warned, however, trees may catch fire with lava pools nearby. Watch out for hostile mobs in the darkness, especially Creepers under the Oak Trees.

History[edit]
When the biome was added, It had no Sacred Oak trees. It was a mountainous biome with generation similar to that of the Overgrown Cliffs biome, but with grass instead of overgrown stone, and pools of water instead of the patches of forest/jungle. It also had a deep blue sky color. In 1.6.4, Sacred Oak trees were added in Sacred Springs, but used Oak Wood because there was no Sacred Oak Wood in 1.6.4. In 1.7.10, the sky color is no longer present, and Sacred Oak Wood replaced Oak Wood on the Sacred Oak trees. In 1.8, the Sacred Springs biome has lost its mountainous terrain, in favor of a flat, darker biome. This can be changed in the biome's config file, simply by changing "VariationAbove" to a higher number. Since BOP 3.0.0, Large Flowering Oak Trees spawn all over the biome. It is removed entirely in 1.13.2 and upwards.

Sapphire is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History

Generation[edit]
Sapphire Ore can be discovered in water based biomes. A current list of these biomes can be found under Sapphire Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Sapphire Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Sapphire drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Sapphire Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Sapphire can be crafted into a Block of Sapphire for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

The Scrubland is a flat savanna biome with occasional low hills. As a savanna, armadillos, horses, warm variant farm animals, and villages spawn here. The ground is peppered with dry grass, desert grass, and purple wildflowers. The only trees are single log spruce and oak shrubs, with oak leaves detached from any logs being scattered about. Spires of packed mud also generate.

Survival[edit]
While plenty of food can be gathered and farmed here, due to the large amount of animals and grass, however building materials, specifically wood, will be a problem early on. For wood, the player has two options. They can either search for a village, and begin growing acacia trees, or grow oak and spruce, gathered from the leaves that make up the scrubs.

History[edit]
It was removed in 1.8, but re-added in 1.13.2 and higher.
The Scrubland was originally split into two biomes, the Scrubland and Wooded Scrubland. At some point before 1.21, the Wooden Scrubland replaced the normal biome, and was renamed to Scrubland.

Seasonal Forests are perpetually autumnal biomes, composed of a mixture of yellow maple, orange maple, red maple, and oak trees with brownish grass. All types of maple leaf piles are located under their respective tree. Patches of dandelions and poppies are found, toadstools also occasionally spawn here, covering the hilly landscape. Reeds spawn in the water portions of the biome. Regular passive mobs such as sheep, cows, chickens, and pigs spawn here. Due to the abundance of food and wood for building, this is a very good biome to live in, and even more so for people who like autumn foliage. There are a total of two biomes in the biome family.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Pumpkin Patch


2 History
3 Gallery

3.1 Old





Variants[edit]
Pumpkin Patch[edit]
The Pumpkin Patch, formally referred to as the Seasonal Pumpkin Patch, is a variant of the Seasonal Forest featuring more yellowish grass, and lots of pumpkins, sprouts, and toadstools.  The ground is littered with oak shrubs and bushes. Occasional giant pumpkins also spawn around the place, and only orange maple trees and orange maple leaf piles spawn here. Oddly enough, sometimes carved pumpkins and even jack-o-lanterns spawn here. 

History[edit]
In 1.7.10, there is a Seasonal Forest Clearing sub-biome that features less trees. It was removed in 1.8.
In 1.6.4, there is a sub-biome called Seasonal Spruce Forest that spawns additional spruce trees. It was removed in 1.7.2.

The Seasonal Orchard also known as the Boreal Forest is a forest made up of yellow autumn trees. It was renamed to the Aspen Glade in BOP Update 18.2.0.16.





Contents

1 Description

1.1 Mobs & NPCs
1.2 History


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
Seasonal Orchard is a Taiga biome with scattered vegetation. The ground has Grass, Ferns, and Toadstools. Yellow Autumn Trees grow in the Seasonal Orchard.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Passive animal mobs and Wolves spawn here. Villages do not spawn.

History[edit]
The gem found in this biome was Amber.
Previous versions of this biome had denser and more varied trees, and included Roses and Flax.
This biome used to feature on the removed panorama loading screen that appears when BOP is installed.
Trivia[edit]
On Earth, boreal forests can be found in cool wet climates between the tundras and temperate zones. They can be found all the way across the northern hemisphere.
If you are using the forestry mod this biome is plains, or meadow, orientation.
In real life, taiga and boreal forests are actually the same biome; they just have different names. However, taigas/boreal forests are diverse depending where they are.

title: Seasons
summary:
Seasons are a major feature in Serene Seasons. Not only do grass and foliage colors change between seasons, but temperatures shift and the types of crops that are in season will also differ.
There are technically 12 seasons in Serene Seasons, with each of the 4 seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, and W...
content:
Seasons are a major feature in Serene Seasons. Not only do grass and foliage colors change between seasons, but temperatures shift and the types of crops that are in season will also differ.
There are technically 12 seasons in Serene Seasons, with each of the 4 seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter) having an Early, Mid, and Late sub-season. Each sub-season lasts for 8 in-game days by default, so a full year lasts for 96 in-game days. The Four Seasons Affect Temperate and Subtropical Biomes like Forests, Plains and Mountains.
However, tropical biomes, such as jungles, stony peaks and savannas will go through Wet and Dry seasons except Deserts. Additionally, in tropical biomes such as Tropical Rainforest, only Summer crops are in season due to the relatively higher temperatures (Other crops can still be grown underground, or using a glass roof to insulate them). Also during the Early/Late Wet or Dry Seasons, weather will act as it normally does in vanilla Minecraft. Any tropical biomes like Jungles will be hot even during winter and the grass will not change to blue and they will not snow.

Contents

1 Subtropical/Temperate Seasons

1.1 Spring
1.2 Summer
1.3 Autumn
1.4 Winter
1.5 Notes


2 Tropical Seasons

2.1 Wet Season
2.2 Dry Season


3 Blocks & Items

3.1 Calendar
3.2 Season Sensor





Subtropical/Temperate Seasons[edit]
Spring[edit]
Spring is the 1st season of the year for temperate biomes.
In Spring, the grass and foliage transitions to a blue-ish green color, and biome temperatures start warming up from Winter towards the end of the season. Winter snows start to melt, and precipitation is also more frequent in Spring. The icon for spring is a pink flower.

Summer[edit]
Summer is the 2nd season of the year for temperate biomes.
In Summer, the grass and foliage mellows out to a yellow-ish green tint. Temperatures are the highest at this time and percipitation steadily decreases after the transition from Spring. Thunderstorms are also more common in summer. The icon for summer is a yellow sun.

Autumn[edit]
Autumn is the 3rd season of the year for temperate biomes.
In Autumn, the grass transitions to a yellow-ish color, while foliage gets a yellow-ish and later an orange-ish tint, which is most vibrant at its peak. Biome temperatures start to fall towards the end of the season leading to Winter. The icon for autumn is an orange maple leaf.

Winter[edit]
Winter is the 4th season of the year for temperate biomes.
In Winter, the grass and foliage fades in color into brown or gray, making plants look dead. Biome temperatures are the lowest, allowing snow to start falling in biomes that normally don't receive any. Precipitation is also more frequent in Winter. The icon for winter is a snowflake. 

Notes[edit]
Evergreen Trees like Fir or Spruce do not get affected by Seasons.
Leaves don't disappear in the winter.
Tropical Seasons[edit]
Wet Season[edit]
The Wet Season is a tropical season affecting tropical biomes (Jungles, Deserts, etc.). It is split up into 3 sub-seasons: Early Wet Season, Mid Wet Season, and Late Wet Season. The Wet Season starts at the beginning of Winter, and ends at the beginning of Summer.
In the Wet Season, the grass and foliage turns to a lush, green color.
In the Mid Wet Season, it can rain in tropical biomes that normally don't receive any.

Dry Season[edit]
The Dry Season is a tropical season affecting tropical biomes (Jungles, Deserts, etc.). It is split up into 3 sub-seasons: Early Dry Season, Mid Dry Season, and Late Dry Season. The Dry Season starts at the beginning of Summer, and ends at the beginning of Winter.
In the Dry Season, the grass and foliage turns to a yellow-ish color.
In the Mid Dry Season, it won't rain in tropical biomes that normally receive it. 

Blocks & Items[edit]
Calendar[edit]
  
The Calendar can be crafted to check the progression of the seasons. It is represented by dots: 1 dot is Early, 2 dots is Mid, and 3 dots is Late. If you are in any tropical biome, the progression of tropical seasons will be seen instead. It is craftable by 8 paper around 1 clock. 

Season Sensor[edit]
  
There is also a Season Sensor, which can be right-clicked to switch between the 4 main seasons and gives off a redstone signal if the season it's set to is currently present in the world.
The strength of the signal correlates to how far it is into the season. At the start of a season, it will have a strength of 1, and increase up to a strength of 15 by the end.

Disclaimer[edit]
Other mods besides Biomes O' Plenty may alter world generation, thereby producing unexpected results when generating worlds with the seeds listed here. Because of this and other mitigating factors, persons who post seeds are not held to any standard of accuracy whatsoever, although submitters are encouraged to be as accurate and concise as possible when adding seed entries. Submitters are encouraged to try not to run mods that may add/remove/modify biomes or otherwise alter the generation of terrain to a great degree (except Biomes O' Plenty, of course) when searching for seeds to add to the repository. Numerical seed entries are preferred, but seeds that contain letters or a mix of numbers and letters are accepted too.
As was said earlier, try to be as accurate and precise as possible with descriptions, although massive paragraphs describing seeds are often unnecessary and annoying, so try to keep the description of seeds short, preferably around 35-50 words per entry. Seeds or descriptions that contain offensive or inappropriate language will be removed. With all that being said, every contribution counts, so edit and add away!

Seeds[edit]
New seed entries should be listed under their corresponding version of Minecraft and BOP. If the version of Minecraft or BOP you are using is not listed, feel free to create a new header for it. To check what version of BOP you are using, go to the Minecraft main menu, click on the Mods button, and locate Biomes O' Plenty in the left sidebar (you may need to scroll to find it). The version number should be listed below the text Biomes O' Plenty in that sidebar.
Copy and use the following code for new entries:

*SEED — DESCRIPTION. <small>Added by ~~~~</small>

Please do not mess up the format of the page. and using the exact BOP build number is strongly recommended, which can be found in the mods settings. 
You can now get to BOP biomes easily in any world using the /bop command, and /locatebiome in 1.16.1+

4770946558198311384 - PLAINS VILLAGE ISLAND Spawn on a relatively large Plains biome island with scattered trees and a small Forest biome in the center of the island, as well as a village nearby. Dozens of small sand.
-7858618268382545908 - SAVANNA ISLAND Spawn on a large Savanna biome island with some Savanna Plateau hills scattered. To the northeast of the island is a very LARGE Extreme Hills biome island with multiple ravines visible.
-5188175755478910039 - BAYOU ISLAND Spawn on a very large Bayou biome island. Wood resources are not a scarcity here! Neither are sheep and cows! Directly southwest of spawn, perhaps a hundred blocks or so, is a small set of Euycalyptus Forest biome islands. Directly behind said islands is a small Jungle biome island, and south of that island is a Rainforest biome island.
1263733433708394450 - LONG PLAINS ISLAND Spawn on quite a long and narrow Plains biome island. There will be one tree on the smaller island right off the northern shore. With Forestry installed, there will be another tree at the southern end of the island. Just off the southern tip of the island there will be a small Gravel Beach island.
-3669518809747573702 - ALPS ISLANDS Spawn right on the very lower edge of an Alps Foothills biome island. Rather large and tall island too, surrounded by other tall Alps Foothills islands. A scattering of fir trees on the island as well, and plenty of llama's to be had!
-3747896763061264549 - SAVANNA AND BRUSHLANDS ISLAND Spawn on the beach of a Savanna biome island. Large and sprawling savanna with quite a lot of acacia trees. Just to the south of spawn, perhaps 200-300 blocks, the island merges into a Brushlands biome. Wood resources are plentiful!
-391946116920438142 - GRASSLANDS ISLAND Spawn on the rolling hills of a Grasslands biome island. With Natura installed, you will find no shortage of the pink Eucalyptus trees added by the Natura mod! To the north is a small Seasonal Forest biome island, and to the east of that is a Roofed Forest biome island split in two by a river.
149438395276413054 - EXTREME HILLS AND SHRUBLANDS ISLAND Spawn at the edge of an Extreme Hills biome island. With Natura installed, you will find no shortage of pink Eucalyptus trees added by the Natura mod! Directly to the east of spawn, the extreme hills merge into a Shrublands biome. The scenery is picturesque!
8337502508641501165 - TAIGA ISLAND WITH VILLAGE Spawn near the edge of a Taiga biome island. This island merges with a Tundra biome directly behind spawn about 100-200 blocks. To the north of spawn, right over a hill, is a quaint little village. With Forestry installed, this village with generate with a Beekeeper's hut, with an Apiarist and an Arborist villager! Chest will have random Forestry loot.
Added by sheesh1991

Rose Quartz - Spawn in Maple Woods biome. Go east and you'll find a village.

A short walk's away is a Wasteland, and an Outback. Further into the Vanilla Desert is a village, and Desert Temple. A couple more Desert-like biomes are around, like a Brushland, and Lush Desert. Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
This biome founds itself on Dirt with exposed areas of Stone and stone-variants. Exposed Coal veins are common. It can contain lakes, and can also have large stretches of forest without any stoney outcrops.

Vegetation[edit]
Trees include Fir and Pine Trees as well as Spruce and Oak from Vanilla Minecraft.  Grasses include Short Grass, Medium Grass, Tall Grass, Wheat Grass, and Damp Grass.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Both Deers and Dragonflies may spawn in this biome.

Survival[edit]
Survival is fairly easy. There is plenty of wood for tools and building, and edible mobs spawn here. It is also possible to make Mossy Stone from the frequent growths of Moss.

The Shrubland biome is composed of low hills with lots of grasses, and no trees. It is populated densely by groups of oak bushes and bush plants. Passive creatures, notably horses, spawn naturally. Surviving here is a bit difficult, there are passive mobs, but the wood is very scarce, because the bushes only have only one block tall. However, the shrubs are a bit hearty, giving the player wood. You need to plant trees here to survive. There is a variant biome, Rocky Shrubland.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Rocky Shrubland
1.2 History


2 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Rocky Shrubland[edit]
The Rocky Shrubland, apparently a new version of the Chaparral, is a variant of the shrubland having less bushes and patches of stone replacing grass. The Chaparral used to have more lush color of grass instead of the regular shrubland color.

History[edit]
When the biome was released, there were a lot less bushes in the biome. There was also a sub-biome called Thick Shrubland that was close to the biome we have today, having more bushes. In 1.7.2 and 1.7.10, the Thick Shrubland sub-biome was removed and made having more bushes.

The Silkglade is a rare swampy biome with patches of cobwebs strewn around its mountainous landscape. Vines drip off of many trees and mushrooms spawn below the tree cover.

Contents

1 Vegetation
2 Mobs & NPCs
3 Features
4 Early Survival
5 History
6 Seeds
7 Gallery



Vegetation[edit]
Willow-shaped oak trees, oak bushes, oak-shaped dead trees and pear-shaped birch trees spawn naturally as well as mushrooms and sparse tall grass.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Spiders replace many hostile mob spawns, but during the day will only be hostile if encountered in the dark.
Passive mobs spawn naturally.

Features[edit]
Cobwebs are strewn about the ground and trees in various places. These are non-renewable, however; they do quicken the access to string and can be crafted into wool making an early bed easily obtainable.

Early Survival[edit]
The Silkglade is not a terribly good first day survival choice because of the spawning primarily consisting of spiders and the common spawning of cobweb patches around the land. This being combined with the partially dead swamp like biome makes the Silkglade a very poor choice for living.

History[edit]
This biome was removed when BOP 1.8 was released. 
It was later re-added back in 1.13.2 and higher under the name Silkglade. It has been removed again in build 1.16.5.
In 1.7.2 and 1.7.10, Silkglade was a sub-biome of the Sludgepit.

List of all the sky and fog colors of the biomes. Colors are in the Hexadecimal format. This page is meant for people who wanna restore old sky/fog colors in newer versions of BOP, unless it still exists. in 1.8.9 - 1.12.2, it can be done in the config files by editing "skyColor" and "fogColor" (in Decimal format, converter mentioned below). However from 1.13.2 and above, it will require editing the source code of BOP, which is not recommended to share. If you wanna convert Hexadecimal to Decimal, you can try converters online like this one. For grass, foliage and water colors, check out the Biomes List. Also from 1.5.2 - 1.7.10, BOP was able to change the sky and fog colors of vanilla biomes, so those are included as well.

Skystone is a pale stone block found exclusively in the Promised Land dimension.

Obtaining[edit]
Skystone can be found under the topsoil of islands in the Promised Lands.
When mined with a pickaxe it drops Skystone Cobblestone, which can then be smelted to form Skystone. However, it is also possible to use the Silk Touch enchantment to mine Skystone directly. It's only crafting use is in Skystone Bricks

Description[edit]
The Sludgepit is a dark, swampy biome with a dense canopy of large trees. Mud, and pools of poison water spawn naturally in this biome.

Vegetation[edit]
Algae and Reeds occupy the water and its edge respectively. Large and small oak trees pop up evenly in and out of the water.
Template:MC and Template:MC litter the dusky green grass where mud has not taken over. Template:MC spawn naturally.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
There are no Template:MC. Template:MC spawn in this biome. Template:MC can spawn in this biome as well, though they are often flooded.

Early Survival[edit]
Surviving the Sludgepit could be easy, but keep in mind that there are no passive mobs in it. Food sources are limited to Template:MC which can be dropped by destroying oak leaves, as well as red and brown mushrooms which can be crafted into Template:MC. Wood is plentiful, and mud balls can also be used as a crafting replacement in many ways as well.

History[edit]
When BOP was released, this biome was originally called Bog. In 1.5.2 it was renamed to Sludgepit because an actual Bog biome was added. Trees for the biome in the code for 1.6.4, 1.7.2 and 1.7.10 are still called Bog Trees. It was removed when 1.8 was released.

Smoldering Grass Block
	
		
		
	
	

	Smoldering Grass Block



Smoldering Grass is found in the Undergarden and Phantasmagoric Inferno biomes in the Nether as well as the Deadlands, and Volcano in the overworld.
If broken with a tool enchanted with Silk Touch, the block itself will be dropped. If shoveled, the block will turn into dirt. If broken by hand, it drops coarse dirt.
This block will burn the player if they walk atop it. Armor enchanted with any level of Fire Protection will allow a player to walk on Smoldering Grass without taking fire damage.

The Snowblossom Grove is a biome similar to the Cherry Blossom Grove, which got removed in 1.20. This biome consists of snowy grass blocks as as surface cover. Little Mossy Cobblestone rocks are scattered across the snowy grass. This biome contains Snowblossom Trees and leaf particles falling from them. It can be found in snowy areas. Grass, Clovers and White Petal flowers spawn here all of the time.

History[edit]
This biome was added in 1.20. The reason why this biome was added is to honor the Cherry Blossom Grove, which was removed due to the Cherry Grove biome being added in vanilla Minecraft.

Trivia[edit]

This biome should mostly spawn near other snowy biomes. The biome is a bit rare.

The Snowy Forest made up of small oak trees with Dying Tree Leaves and lots of snow.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery

2.1 Current





Description[edit]
The terrain consists of small hills and shallow water pools, many frozen over.

Vegetation[edit]
Dying Oaks covered in snow make up the forest, with little other vegetation. Violets provide spots of colour, and Sugar Cane may spawn beside ponds.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Common passive mobs will spawn in this biome.

Survival[edit]
There is plenty of wood as well as passive mobs for food. Farming will be more difficult as water will freeze if open to the sky.

History[edit]
When this biome was added, it was formerly called the Frost Forest, and had a white sky color and had bluish-white colored leaves and grass. In 1.8.9, It was renamed to Snowy Forest, the sky color was removed and the leaves' color and grass color was changed to brown.

The Snowy Tundra is a cold biome that was added in a prerelease for 1.0.

Description[edit]
The Snowy Tundra is uncommon with rare spruce trees. No peaceful mobs other than polar bears spawn. At night, 80% of skeletons spawned under direct sunlight will be strays.

Mobs and NPCs[edit]
Only polar bears spawn here in the day. Villages can spawn here, and the crops are dried out.

History[edit]
Villages previously did not spawn here, but they now do as of 1.14. Note that BOP is not at 1.14 yet.

Spectral Moss is a block that is currently unobtainable in Survival Mode. It is possible that it was intended to be used for the Spectral Garden, the End biome.

Obtaining[edit]
Can only be mined by a pickaxe, but will drop end stone instead. If mined without pickaxe, it will drop nothing. If mined with a pickaxe with Silk Touch enchantment, it will drop the block itself.

Trivia[edit]
The appearence of this block suggest to be a block to be generated in The End.
This appears to be the End's equivalent of a regular grass block, similarly to how the Nether has its Overgrown Netherrack.
This block will create green particles when mined, unlike other blocks which create particles based on their appearance.
It was removed in 1.13.2.

The Spring Water Bucket is an Amethyst Bucket that has been filled with Spring Water. 
Spring Water could be found naturally occurring in the Hot Springs biome. It has a distinct light blue color and can also occur underground (as long as it is in the Hot Springs biome). It will not last infinitely - infinite water sources cannot be made with this. Spring Water gives the Regeneration effect, which heals players, as well as a new Nourishment effect, which restores hunger.

Collection[edit]
Spring water can only be picked up using a vanilla bucket, as attempting to pick it up using an Amethyst Bucket will result in a bucket of normal water. It should be noted that unlike vanilla water, Spring Water cannot be made into an infinite pool of any form and therefore there is a finite yet still extremely large quantity of it.
Since the Amethyst Bucket got removed, the Spring Water can not be picked up by a regular Bucket.

Description[edit]
Spruce Woods is a sub-biome of the Forest Biome, containing some Spruce trees. Filled with lots of grass, Berry Bushes, Dandelions and Bluebells. Oak trees, ferns and sprouts do spawn here, but lakes and ponds are a rare find in this biome. This biome has different variant spruce trees, however contains only 1 variant oak tree.

Tips for survival[edit]
These are easy to play in survival, using berries as food and the animals spawning in the biome. There is a variety of wood so you can build more diverse houses easily.

Mobs and NPCs[edit]
Sheep, chicken, pigs and all other vanilla animals spawn here. Since villages don't spawn here, villagers don't too.

History[edit]
It doesn't exist after BOP 1.7.10, and it was added in 1.3.2.

The Steppe is a sparse biome with a mixture of sandy grass, and dried sand with different coloured patches. This biome is not present in 1.16.4


Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Gallery



Description[edit]
The Steppe is notably tan brown in hue, with almost no vegetation, and absolutely no trees.

Vegetation[edit]
Very little. Dead Bushes, Grass, and Desert Grass can spawn.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Horses and other passive mobs frequently spawn here. Llamas are very common in this biome.

Survival[edit]
The lack of trees, food, and water make this biome an unpleasant starting spot. Players who wish to settle here will need to track down resources from other biomes and cart them back. The possibilities of Donkeys and Llama may help in this task.

Tanzanite is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O'Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History



Generation[edit]
Although Tanzanite can be found in snowy biomes, it is not found in Alps. A current list of these biomes can be found under Tanzanite Biomes.

Obtaining[edit]
An Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Tanzanite Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Tanzanite drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Tanzanite Ore cannot be smelted.

Use[edit]
9 Tanzanite can be crafted into a Block of Tanzanite for storage or decoration. These stack to 64.

This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.

The temperate rainforest biome is a forest filled with tall redwoods conifers and ferns.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 History


2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
Dense scrub and huge spruce trees in the shape of conifers grow out of standard dirt blocks. The grass and Oak Leaves in this biome are a light green.

Vegetation[edit]
Oak trees are most prominent, but there are also a lot of willow trees and redwoods. Ferns andns and Tall Ferns grow abundantly.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Common passive mobs spawn here.

Survival[edit]
This biome is a pretty good place to start because of the large quantity of wood. Even though there's plenty of wood, survival can still be tough as most of the trees are very tall and hard to chop down. The leaves provide a lot of shade, so zombies and skeletons can hide beneath the canopy and survive the sun to attack the player.

History[edit]
2x2 trees used to appear in this biome before 1.8. In late 1.12.2, Redwood Wood replaced Oak Wood on the big trees. In 1.15.2, it was made flatter with huge patches of water and no Redwood Trees due to the Temperate Rainforest Hills sub-biome.

Unfortunately, it got removed in 1.16.4

Trivia[edit]
In real life, Temperate Rainforests can also be deciduous and receive heavy rainfall.
In the world, they appear in the Pacific Northwest, New Zealand, much of the Gaelic parts of the British Isles, and Korea.

title: TerraBlender
summary: TerraBlender is a mod created by Glitchfiend that serves as a dependency mod for versions of Biomes O Plenty over 1.17.1. It creates an easier way to add biomes, using regions, which makes it so only modded biomes can spawn in a specific area, and vanilla biomes can only spawn in a specific area, es...
content:
TerraBlender is a mod created by Glitchfiend that serves as a dependency mod for versions of Biomes O' Plenty over 1.17.1. It creates an easier way to add biomes, using regions, which makes it so only modded biomes can spawn in a specific area, and vanilla biomes can only spawn in a specific area, essentially "blending" the terrain. This mod is also used by Oh The Biomes You'll Go!, Promenade, and several other mods.
If TerraBlender is not installed, an error message will appear saying that Biomes O' Plenty failed to load and Minecraft will not load properly. TerraBlender can be used to create your own biome mod.

The thicket is a biome covered in small oak trees and shrubs with thorns spread about,these biomes look a lot like the Shrubland. Allium flowers, a rare vanilla flower normally only found in the flower forest, appear frequently in this biome. Tallgrass is a bit rarer in this biome. One could easily avoid the thorns making this a good biome to live in, as there is plenty of wood, passive mobs spawn here, and the thorns could be used as traps. In addition, the wood is abundant and can be used to build a shelter and to make beds. In short, survival is very easy here. However, it was removed in 1.8.9

History[edit]
When it was added, it had green grass and foliage color. In 1.7.2, it was changed to have a darker shade of gray instead. It was removed in 1.8.9.

title: Thirst
summary: Thirst is one of the major components of Tough As Nails. Its similar to hunger, in that it will drop from moving around a lot. You also cannot sprint if your thirst is too low, and you will die of dehydration on Hard/Hardcore difficulties. There are a variety of ways to quench your thirst, from cant...
content:
Thirst is one of the major components of Tough As Nails. It's similar to hunger, in that it will drop from moving around a lot. You also cannot sprint if your thirst is too low, and you will die of dehydration on Hard/Hardcore difficulties. There are a variety of ways to quench your thirst, from canteens to juices.
The canteen is the most basic item for restoring thirst. It can be crafted with just 6 pieces of leather, making it ideal for early-game survival. However, water collected with the canteen will always be dirty, and have a very high chance of giving the Thirst status effect.
The Thirst status effect will make your thirst drop at a faster rate, similar to the Hunger effect that can occur from eating uncooked foods and other items.
To prevent this, you can collect water with glass bottles, and filter/clean it. All water collected by water bottles will be dirty at the start, and you must filter it with a charcoal filter before you can clean it by boiling it in a furnace.
Another way to get clean water is with a rain collector. They will fill up gradually when it rains, and any water collected from them will be clean.
You can also make various juices with clean water, sugar, and various fruits/vegetables. They restore more thirst than water, so it's a great option if you plan on travelling or won't be near water for a while.
In addition, potions and buckets of milk also restore thirst. Here is a full list of items that can restore thirst, as well as how much they restore:

Tiny cacti are plants that spawn in desert and desert-like biomes, such as the lush desert, Vanilla desert, and mesa. It can be smelted into cactus green via a furnace. Picking it up doesn't require a pair of shears.

Usages[edit]
Tiny cacti can be smelted into cactus green. Tiny cacti can not be placed in a flower pot, vanilla cacti must be used instead.

Trivia[edit]
The tiny cactus resembles a real-life cactus. Tiny cactus will sometimes generate without their flowers, or the flowers will fall off. This is a completely random chance.

History[edit]
The Tiny cactus was added in 1.12.2 removed in 1.13.2, and later re-added in 1.20.2, but with a completely different texture.

The Toadstool is a type of mushroom that can be found in several biomes, such as the Fen, Shield, and Coniferous Forest. It can be used as decoration, in Shroom Salad or to make Shroom Powder.
The Toadstool, along with the Portobello, Glowshroom, and Blue Milk Cap, are all fungi added by Biomes o' Plenty.
Since 1.15.2, Toadstools can be grown into Giant Toadstools.

Topaz is a biome-specific Gemstone introduced with Biomes O' Plenty. It appears as an ore, an item, and a decorative block.

Contents

1 Generation
2 Obtaining
3 Use

3.1 Crafting recipes:


4 History



Generation[edit]
Topaz Ore can be discovered in cooler, lush, hot/tropical or jungle regions. A current list of these biomes can be found under Topaz Biomes. 

Obtaining[edit]
A Iron Pickaxe or better is required to mine Topaz Ore. A Silk Touch Pickaxe can be used to collect the block of ore rather than the Topaz drop. The ore drops one gem with an unenchanted pickaxe. With fortune, the ore can drop up to four gems, one extra per level of fortune. Topaz Ore cannot be smelted.The Ore is a common specimen in Minecraft and is found in many biomes and can be mined with an iron pickaxe or above.

Use[edit]
9 Topaz can be crafted into a Block of Topaz for storage or decoration. These stack in 64.

Tough As Nails is a survival-oriented mod created by Glitchfiend, Adubbz and Forstride. It's focused on making the game more challanging and difficult by adding in more dangers, such as thirst, temperature and limited health.
It has been discontinued since late 2019.

Effects with this mod[edit]
Body Temperature will be affected by biomes in this mod, for example (with no config changes) Alps will be -10, Xeric Shrubland will be +10, etc.

Features[edit]
Thirst: Similar to hunger it drops from moving around and can be quenched by drinking different types of drinks.
Body Temperature: The Body Temperature is controlled by the Biome Temperature, Day-/Nighttime and more...
Tweaks: Tough As Nails makes tweaks to various vanilla features, including loot table balancing.

As part of modified world generation, Biomes O' Plenty generates a number of new varieties of trees. Some were designed to make the biome more realistic, for example, Palm Trees in tropical biomes. Others, such as Magic Trees, were added to fantasy biomes for players who want to do a little make-believe. Trees have a log block, a leaf block, and planks, as well as slabs, stairs, pressure plates, buttons, fences, fence gates, signs, boats, chest boats, and doors. They also have saplings.
Each of the regular tree types can be cut down for wood and planks, and the planks can be crafted into stairs and slabs. They come in a variety of colors, which make them excellent for avid builders. Leaves can also be harvested with shears or broken for occasional saplings. Additionally, logs can be stripped to create barkless versions of their respective species.

The Tropics is a very rare biome filled with somewhat mountainous islands covered in Blue Hydrangeas, Pink Hibiscus, Flowering Oak Trees, and Palm Trees. Occasional jungle trees, bamboo stalks and jungle shrubs also spawn here. Sandy beaches, shallow seas, bright green grass and well-lit skies make this a great find. The beaches here are composed of white sand, instead of regular sand. Jungle Temples generate here, like most other tropical-themed biomes in the mod. Parrots can spawn in this biome. This biome is very easy to survive in, due to the passive mobs and wood.

The Tundra is a hilly biome covered in red maple scrub and dead scrub with lots of ferns and mossy rocks. Reeds can be found in the lakes of this biome. This biome was created to resemble the tundra of Siberia and northern North America, both inhospitable places. Gravel usually spawns near the shoreline in this biome. Survival is tough here, with the only wood coming from the single oak log in every bush, and no actual trees present. There are only 2 sources of meat - Zombies' Rotten Flesh and Rabbit's Meat, but these are not ideal and hard to get. Wolves and foxes spawn here.
There used to be a snowy variant of the biome called Snowy Tundra.

Trivia[edit]
This biome used to exist in vanilla Minecraft prior to Beta 1.8, though with major differences.

title: Turkey
summary:
Turkey are passive mobs that generally spawn in temperate forest biomes, as well as some colder biomes. They randomly spawn as either a hen (Female) or tom (Male).
Additionally, Turkey can be tempted/bred using wheat, beetroot, pumpkin, or melon seeds.
When killed, mature turkey drop Turkey Legs, wh...
content:
Turkey are passive mobs that generally spawn in temperate forest biomes, as well as some colder biomes. They randomly spawn as either a hen (Female) or tom (Male).
Additionally, Turkey can be tempted/bred using wheat, beetroot, pumpkin, or melon seeds.
When killed, mature turkey drop Turkey Legs, which can be eaten raw, but they will give the Hunger effect, or they can cooked to be eaten safely and restore additional hunger.


Additionally, chicken spawns are removed from biomes that turkey spawn in, so it doesn't feel redundant, and turkey have a greater chance of spawning.
(NOTE: This feature can be disabled in the configuration settings!)

content:
Umbran Trees are huge dark purple trees similar to fir trees. They're found in the Ominous Woods biome. The tree can be grown either using just one sapling, or four saplings arranged in a 2x2 grid. When the tree is grown with only one sapling, it becomes a short tree with very few leaves. When the tree is grown with four saplings in a 2x2 grid, it becomes a tall tree with lots of logs and leaves drooping down. The planks of the tree are a purple-bluish color. The doors and trapdoors have faces on them.
In older versions, they were more purple and grew in a spruce tree or oak tree shape. They could also have Umbran Tree Moss growing on them. Before 1.8 they were called Dark Trees and had different textures.

The Undergrowth, formerly Undergarden, is a densely filled nether biome with lots of bramble, sprouts, burning blossoms, and occasional hellbark trees. Willow vines hang from the ceiling, and spore particles meander around the green air. This biome can be much more dangerous than other Nether biomes (despite the lack of lava) if you are not properly prepared. This lush green area may look extremely inviting if you've been on the run from Ghasts, but many of the plants are very dangerous. Hoglins and Magma Cubes spawn in this biome.

History[edit]

This page describes a removed feature.This feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.
A food crafted from a bowl, a Potato, a Carrot and Wild Carrots (before 1.9.4) or a Turnip (1.9.4 and after). They fill 6 hunger (3 shanks).
Wild carrots can not be farmed, while potatoes and carrots are not found in the wild (unless you consider villages the wild) making this food somewhat awkward, but filling.
Veggie Salad was removed in BOP 1.12.2-7.0.1.2355, just like other Salads.

The Visceral Heap is a Nether biome made of Flesh with Flesh Tendons hanging from the ceiling and bone columns on the ground. Hair, Pus Bubbles and Eyebulbs frequently spawn around the place. Porous Flesh also occasionally replaces flesh on the surface. Large strands of flesh protrude in this biome, with shroomlights in the center and flesh tendons hanging from below. Liquid blood lakes and springs spawn in this gross place.
First of all, you shouldn't be attempting to survive here, unless you are an incredibly experienced player with good knowledge of the Nether. The Nether is not the place to be surviving, so make sure you bring a lot of cobblestone to protect against Ghast fireballs.

History[edit]
As of early April 2016, Nether Biomes have not been re-added to 1.9 and 1.8.9 BoP, though the programmers are planning to bring them back. They are in 1.7.10 and earlier, though.
However, in version 1.11.2+ all nether biomes except Boneyard are re-added to BOP.



1.6.4

The Bloody Heap is added to the mod.


1.8

Bloody Heap and all other Nether biomes are removed from the mod.


1.11.2

Bloody Heap is re-added and renamed to Visceral Heap.


1.13.2

Eyebulbs and Blood springs no longer spawn in this biome.


1.16.1

The fog color was changed, and large flesh strands were added in the biome.


1.17.1

Hair, Pus Bubbles, and Flesh Tendons were added. Blood is re-added.


1.19.2

Eyebulbs spawn once again.

The Volcano is a rare biome made of smooth basalt. It is usually mountainous, and there are lots of lava lakes surrounded by magma blocks and stone. Ash particles similar to the ones in the Basalt Deltas spawn here. There is almost always a Volcanic Plains biome surrounding it. Survival in this biome would be difficult due to the lack of trees, impossibility of farming, and lack of passive mobs. The lava and magma blocks also provide an additional hazard.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Volcanic Plains


2 History
3 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Volcanic Plains[edit]
The Volcanic Plains is a biome made of black sand that spawns around the Volcano. There are patches of grass blocks and sprouts growing on them.

History[edit]
When BOP was released, the ground was also composed of Stone. In 1.6.4, Volcano's ground was changed from Stone to Ash Stone. In 1.7.10, it was changed to be an ocean sub-biome and was made more mountainous to resemble real-life volcanoes. In 1.8, the ground was changed once again to Ash Blocks and it was renamed to Volcanic Island. In 1.13.2, Volcanic Island was renamed back to Volcano and huge patches of Magma Blocks are added. In 1.16.1, Ash Blocks were replaced with Basalt blocks, and in 1.17.1 they were replaced with Smooth Basalt blocks.

The Wasteland is a hard, cruel and inhospitable biome made of dried salt. Dead trees spawn here and the only vegetation is scattered patches of dead grass and desert grass. No passive or neutral mobs spawn here. Hostiles still spawn at night and in unlit areas, but creepers do not spawn. Husks spawn instead of zombies. Survival here is very, very difficult. Prior to 1.13, the dead wood found at the surface is only useful as fuel, rendering it almost impossible to survive here. Even after 1.13, it will still be difficult, as the wood in the area is still very scarce. Due to the lack of flora and fauna, food will be a big problem. You will either have to fish for food, or make yourself a nether portal and find food in the Nether.
There are a total of two biomes in the family.

Contents

1 Variants

1.1 Wasteland Steppe


2 History
3 Gallery



Variants[edit]
Wasteland Steppe[edit]
Wasteland Steppes are variants that generate at higher elevations within the regular wasteland.

History[edit]
In earlier versions of BOP, this biome had dirt spikes coming out of the ground, and the water was green. Although in the 1.8/1.9 update of the mod, the random spikes of dirt appear to have been removed and the dirt color has changed to a darker black. In 1.12.2, the color of the water was changed from green to brown. In 1.16.4 - 1.19.2, the wooded wasteland variant biome existed, but it was merged with the regular wasteland in 1.19.3.

Cattails and sugarcane spawn around the coast. Reeds and watergrass can be found in the water, along with inundated patches of seagrass. Exploring is mainly safe because there isn't anything that can hurt you aside from mobs.

title: Wild Carrots
summary: Wild carrots are a food item that can only be found in the wild. There are no seeds that allow you to farm them. Wild carrots appear similar to farmed vanilla carrots when found. content:
Wild carrots are a food item that can only be found in the wild. There are no seeds that allow you to farm them. Wild carrots appear similar to farmed vanilla carrots when found. In the inventory, it appears as a bundle of white carrots. It heals 2 1/2 hunger, but deals Weakness for ten seconds. They can be used in the recipe for Veggie Salad. Wild carrots can be found in many biomes, including Jade Cliffs. However you are not able to farm wild carrots.Wild carrots are hard to find, especially in desperate situations.
As of 1.9.4, wild carrots seem to have been removed. Veggie Salad is now made with a Turnip instead.

content:
Wild Rice is a plant and food ingredient found in the Land of Lakes biome. It is not yet implemented as an arable feature, but is used in the Bowl of Rice recipe. Harvesting it with Shears will always yield a rice plant, while breaking it with the player's hand (as of 1.12) will only occasionally drop rice plants.

title: Willow Tree
summary: Willow Trees are lush trees found in the Wetland and Bayou. Their shape is similar to oak trees that grow in the swamp biome. They can grow two types of plants on their tree, Willow Vines and Spanish Moss. Willow Trees with Spanish Moss can be found in the Bayou naturally, while ones with Willow Vin...
content:
Willow Trees are lush trees found in the Wetland and Bayou. Their shape is similar to oak trees that grow in the swamp biome. They can grow two types of plants on their tree, Willow Vines and Spanish Moss. Willow Trees with Spanish Moss can be found in the Bayou naturally, while ones with Willow Vines can be found in the Wetland biome. If grown via saplings, the tree can grow either Spanish Moss or Willow Vines. The color of the planks is a light green. Doors and trapdoors are screen doors with vegetation over it.

Withered Abyss is a very dark Nether biome with a black fog and the ground is made out of blackstone with some very small patches of obsidian and crying obsidian. Blackstone bulbs are scattered across the ground and it lacks piles of glowstone. Only endermen and wither skeletons spawn in this biome. If you are going to the Nether for the first time, make sure to avoid this biome, because it is very dark to see unless you bring some torches or glowstone. Crying obsidian and blackstone bulbs, however, do provide a very small amount of light. Also make sure to wear some armor, because wither skeletons spawn naturally and can easily take you out without armor. Wither skeletons along with no glowstone piles will make it very dangerous to travel through this biome due to wither skeleton's wither effect and almost complete darkness. Endermen are fine unless you look in their eyes.

Trivia[edit]
Withered Abyss is the only biome that lacks piles of glowstone.
If grass and leaves are placed in the Withered Abyss, they will be black instead of yellow.
History[edit]
It was added in 1.16.1, originally called Shadowlands, but it was quickly renamed to Withered Abyss due to Shadowlands being the same name of the World of Warcraft (WoW) expansion.[1]

The Woodlands biome is a basic forest biome.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 Old Growth


2 History
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
This area is very similar to the Vanilla forest biome, although some aesthetic changes like leaf color, fallen logs and toadstools have been added. There are also no Birch Trees in this biome. Woodland Mansions can spawn in this biome.

Vegetation[edit]
Basic Oak Trees make up the foliage, and there are lots of Dead Leaf Piles beneath them. Small plants include: Poppies, Wheat Grass, Flat Mushrooms, Flax, Oxeye Daisies, Shrubs, and the occasional Berry Bush.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Both Villages and Woodland Mansions can spawn here. Common passive mobs spawn in Woodland.

Survival[edit]
It is one of the easiest biomes for survival due to the plentiful supply of wood and logs. Like other forest biomes, farm animals are common, but can be hard to track in the dense biome. It is a great biome for survival beginners, but beware of the Poison Ivy that can spawn here.

Old Growth[edit]
The Old Growth Woodland is the successor of the Dense Forest, made up of many fancy oaks, and cannot generate mansions.

History[edit]
This biome it was removed in 1.16.4. However, it was re-added in 1.16.5.

The Xeric Shrubland biome is made up of small hills of sand and dirt with grass, flowers, dead shrubs, and cacti littered about.

Contents

1 Description

1.1 Vegetation
1.2 Mobs & NPCs
1.3 Survival
1.4 Seeds

1.4.1 1.9
1.4.2 1.10




2 Trivia
3 Gallery



Description[edit]
The Xeric Shrubland is a type of desert biome. The ground is made up of sand, grass blocks, and acacia leaves. There seems to be a fair number of small water lakes.

Vegetation[edit]
Small Acacia trees and Cacti may occur here, alongside a range of scrub: Tiny Cacti, Template:MC, Template:MC, and Bromeliads.

Mobs & NPCs[edit]
Template:Passive mob do not seem to spawn here. Template:MC spawn in this biome.

Survival[edit]
Survival in this biome is somewhat easy. Trees and farm plants are easy to grow because of the abundance of shrubs, grass, dirt, and water. Farm animals do not spawn even on the grass, so if animals are desired they must be brought from adjacent biomes. Hills are generally too small to build a house on, therefore, it is difficult to see an enemy coming, or indeed rush them or run away.

Trivia[edit]
This biome appears to be exceedingly rare, despite being one of the largest terrestrial biomes on Earth.
This biome was added as part of a community poll for biome ideas.
This biome is not present in 1.16.3 and possibly merged to the Lush Desert, along with the Outback and Oasis.
